title.zh: 卷一百八十八 列傳第一百十三 楊時朱孫
title.en: Volume 188 Biographies 113: Yang, Shi, Zhu and Grandsons
title.raw: 卷一百八十八 列傳第一百十三 楊時朱孫 Volume 188 Biographies 113: Yang, Shi, Zhu and Grandsons

sentences.zh: 楊時朱孫

translations.literal: Yang, Zhu, and their grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of the Yang, Zhu, and Sun lines.

sentences.zh: 楊行密，字化源，廬州合淝人。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi, style name Huayuan, was a native of Hefei in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi, whose style name was Huayuan, came from Hefei in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，與群兒戲，常為旗幟戰陣狀。

translations.literal: He lost his parents young; when playing with other boys, he would often arrange flags and battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he would play war games with other boys, setting out flags and mock battle lines.

sentences.zh: 年二十，亡入盜中，刺史鄭綮捕得，異其貌，曰：「而且富貴，何為作賊？」

translations.literal: At age twenty he fled and joined a band of robbers; the prefect Zheng Zhen captured him, was struck by his appearance, and said, "You are destined for wealth and rank—why play the thief?"
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he ran off and joined a band of robbers. Prefect Zheng Zhen caught him, marveled at his looks, and said, "You are clearly born for wealth and rank—why turn bandit?"

sentences.zh: 縱之。

translations.literal: He released him.
translations.idiomatic: He let him go.

sentences.zh: 與裏人田頵、陶雅、劉威善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with his fellow townsmen Tian Jun, Tao Ya, and Liu Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He became close friends with fellow townsfolk Tian Jun, Tao Ya, and Liu Wei.

sentences.zh: 僖宗在蜀，刺史遣通章行在，日走三百里，如約而還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong was in Shu, the prefect sent him to deliver a memorial to the imperial camp; he traveled three hundred li a day and returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xizong was in Shu, the prefect sent him to carry dispatches to the court-in-exile; he covered three hundred li a day and returned exactly when promised.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權寇廬、壽間，刺史募殺賊，差首級為賞，行密以功補隊長。

translations.literal: When Qin Zongquan raided between Luzhou and Shouzhou, the prefect recruited men to kill bandits, setting rewards by the number of heads; Xingmi was made squad captain for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Zongquan raided the Luzhou–Shouzhou region, the prefect offered bounties for bandit heads; Xingmi earned promotion to squad captain for his kills.

sentences.zh: 都將忌之，俾出戍。

translations.literal: The commander resented him and had him posted to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander envied him and sent him out on frontier duty.

sentences.zh: 將行，都將問所乏，對曰：「我須公頭！」

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the commander asked what he lacked; he replied, "I need your head!"
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure the commander asked what he needed; Xingmi answered, "Your head!"

sentences.zh: 即斬之，自為八營都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: He beheaded him at once and made himself commander of the eight camps' military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He struck off the man's head on the spot and proclaimed himself overall commander of the eight camps.

sentences.zh: 刺史走，淮南節度使高駢因表為廬州刺史。

translations.literal: The prefect fled; the Huainan military governor Gao Pian thereupon memorialized to appoint him prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect fled, and Huainan governor Gao Pian memorialized the throne to make Xingmi prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃以田頵為八營都將，陶雅為左沖山將，討定鄉盜。

translations.literal: He then made Tian Jun commander of the eight camps, Tao Ya left Chongshan general, and pacified local bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Tian Jun to command the eight camps and Tao Ya as left Chongshan general, and they put down local banditry.

sentences.zh: 駢將呂用之恐行密不可制，遣俞公楚以兵五千屯合淝，名討黃巢而陰圖之。

translations.literal: Gao Pian's officer Lü Yongzhi, fearing Xingmi could not be controlled, sent Yu Gongchu with five thousand troops to camp at Hefei, nominally to attack Huang Chao but secretly plotting against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian's lieutenant Lü Yongzhi, uneasy that Xingmi might slip his control, sent Yu Gongchu with five thousand men to encamp at Hefei—ostensibly to fight Huang Chao, but in secret to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 行密擊殺公楚。

translations.literal: Xingmi attacked and killed Gongchu.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi attacked and killed Gongchu.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權遣弟度淮取舒城，行密破走之。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan sent his younger brother across the Huai to take Shucheng; Xingmi defeated and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan sent a younger brother across the Huai to seize Shucheng; Xingmi routed him and forced his retreat.

sentences.zh: 時張敖據壽州，許據滁州，與行密挐戰。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Ao held Shouzhou and Xu held Chuzhou, and they grappled in battle with Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ao held Shouzhou and Xu held Chuzhou, and both clashed repeatedly with Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 又舒人陳儒攻刺史高澞，澞來告難，行密未能定。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Chen Ru of Shuzhou attacked the prefect Gao Yu; Yu came to report the crisis, and Xingmi could not settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Chen Ru of Shuzhou besieged Prefect Gao Yu, who appealed for help; Xingmi could not yet resolve the crisis.

sentences.zh: 賊吳回、李本逐澞，據其城，行密虜之，取舒州，為所奪。

translations.literal: The bandits Wu Hui and Li Ben drove out Yu and seized the city; Xingmi captured them and took Shuzhou, but it was wrested away again.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits Wu Hui and Li Ben expelled Yu and seized the city. Xingmi captured them and took Shuzhou, only to lose it again.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，張敖遣將魏虔攻廬州，大將李神福、田頵破之楮城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Zhang Ao sent the general Wei Qian to attack Luzhou; the great generals Li Shenfu and Tian Jun defeated him at Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi year 2, Zhang Ao sent Wei Qian against Luzhou; Li Shenfu and Tian Jun crushed his force at Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 畢師鐸、秦彥攻高駢，呂用之以駢命署行密行軍司馬，督其兵進援。

translations.literal: Bi Shiduo and Qin Yan attacked Gao Pian; Lü Yongzhi, in Pian's name, appointed Xingmi acting army marshal and ordered his troops forward in relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi Shiduo and Qin Yan attacked Gao Pian, Lü Yongzhi appointed Xingmi acting army marshal in Pian's name and marched his forces to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 客袁襲說行密曰：「高公耄昏，妖人用權，彥乃以逆除暴，熾其亂。

translations.literal: His guest Yuan Xi urged Xingmi, saying, "Lord Gao is senile and muddled; sorcerers hold power. Yan merely replaces tyranny with rebellion and fans the chaos.
translations.idiomatic: His adviser Yuan Xi told him, "Lord Gao is senile and befuddled, and sorcerers rule in his name. Yan only trades one tyrant for another rebel and feeds the disorder.

sentences.zh: 公亟應，必得其地。」

translations.literal: If you respond at once, you are sure to gain his territory."
translations.idiomatic: Answer the call now and you will surely win his territory."

sentences.zh: 行密乃檄部州，裒兵而東，次天長，而揚州陷。

translations.literal: Xingmi then issued orders to his prefectures, gathered troops, and marched east; he halted at Tianchang, but Yangzhou had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi mustered his forces and marched east, halting at Tianchang—by which time Yangzhou had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 行密薄城而屯，用之以兵屬之。

translations.literal: Xingmi drew near the city and encamped; Yongzhi placed troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi camped close beneath the walls, and Yongzhi placed additional troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 彥以騎兵背城戰，行密臥帳中，令曰：「賊近，報我。」

translations.literal: Yan fought with cavalry with his back to the city; Xingmi lay in his tent and ordered, "When the enemy draws near, report to me."
translations.idiomatic: Yan met him with cavalry backed against the city wall. Xingmi lay in his tent and said, "Tell me when the enemy is close."

sentences.zh: 俄而陷一屯，別將李宗禮入曰：「兵相迫，戰且不利，請堅壁，徐引歸可也。」

translations.literal: Soon one camp was overrun; the deputy commander Li Zongli entered and said, "The armies are pressing each other and the fight goes badly—please hold the walls and withdraw slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Soon one camp fell. Deputy Li Zongli came in and said, "The lines are tangled and we are losing ground—hold the fortifications and pull back gradually."

sentences.zh: 李濤怒曰：「以順去逆，何眾寡為！

translations.literal: Li Tao angrily said, "When the loyal strike the rebel, what matter numbers!
translations.idiomatic: Li Tao snapped, "When righteousness strikes down rebellion, what do numbers matter!

sentences.zh: 今尚何歸，願以所部前死。」

translations.literal: Where is there to retreat now? I ask to lead my command forward to die."
translations.idiomatic: There is nowhere left to retreat—I will lead my men to die in the van."

sentences.zh: 行密喜，益甲出戰，俘殺如藉，彥軍不出。

translations.literal: Xingmi was pleased, sent more armor into battle, and took and killed prisoners in heaps; Yan's army did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was delighted, threw in fresh troops, and piled up captives and corpses until Yan's men would not leave the city.

sentences.zh: 會駢死，襲勸行密舉軍縞素，大臨三日。

translations.literal: When Pian died, Xi urged Xingmi to dress the whole army in mourning white and hold a grand mourning for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Pian died, Xi urged Xingmi to dress the army in white mourning and hold a three-day state funeral.

sentences.zh: 進攻城，未能下。

translations.literal: He pressed the siege but could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the siege but could not bring the city down.

sentences.zh: 用之將張審晟詭伏西壕，殺閽者，啟外兵，彥軍疲，守邏皆潰去，行密入據揚州。

translations.literal: Yongzhi's officer Zhang Shensheng lay in ambush by the western moat, killed the gate guards, and admitted the outside troops; Yan's army was exhausted, the wall defenders all fled, and Xingmi entered and seized Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi's man Zhang Shensheng ambushed by the western moat, slew the gate guards, and let the besiegers in. Yan's weary defenders broke and ran, and Xingmi took Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未閱月，孫儒奄至，兵銳甚。

translations.literal: Within less than a month Sun Ru arrived suddenly, his troops very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Before a month had passed Sun Ru appeared without warning, his army fresh and fierce.

sentences.zh: 襲見行密曰：「公之入，以少擊眾，室家未完。

translations.literal: Xi saw Xingmi and said, "When you entered you struck the many with the few, and your household is not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xi told him, "You seized the city with a small force against a large one, and your household is not yet secure.

sentences.zh: 若外被重圍，情見勢殆，不如避之。」

translations.literal: If you are heavily besieged from without, your plight will show and the situation grow desperate—better to withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: If enemies close in from outside, your weakness will show and the position will turn desperate—you should withdraw."

sentences.zh: 行密執海陵鎮遏使高霸殺之，並其眾，輦所收財歸於廬。

translations.literal: Xingmi seized Gao Ba, the Hailing garrison suppressor, killed him, absorbed his troops, and carted the wealth he had gathered back to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi seized and executed Gao Ba, the Hailing garrison commander, absorbed his troops, and hauled his hoarded wealth back to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是，朱全忠自為淮南節度使，遣將張廷範致命，而授行密副使，以行軍司馬李璠知留後。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhu Quanzhong made himself Huainan military governor, sent the general Zhang Tingfan to deliver his commission, appointed Xingmi deputy commissioner, and made the acting army marshal Li Fan provisional governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong then claimed the Huainan governorship himself, sent Zhang Tingfan with his commission, named Xingmi deputy commissioner, and left acting marshal Li Fan in charge at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密大怒，廷範、璠不敢入。

translations.literal: Xingmi was furious; Tingfan and Fan dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was furious, and neither Tingfan nor Fan dared enter the city.

sentences.zh: 全忠更請以行密知觀察留後。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then requested instead that Xingmi serve as provisional observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then petitioned to have Xingmi made provisional observation commissioner instead.

sentences.zh: 當此時，孫儒強，赫然有吞吳、越意。

translations.literal: At this time Sun Ru was strong and plainly intended to swallow Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru was then at the height of his power and plainly aimed to swallow Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 行密欲遁保海陵，襲勸還廬州，治兵為後計，行密乃還。

translations.literal: Xingmi wished to flee and hold Hailing; Xi urged him to return to Luzhou, drill troops, and plan for the future, and Xingmi went back.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi wanted to slip away to Hailing, but Xi urged a return to Luzhou to rebuild his forces for the long fight, and Xingmi agreed.

sentences.zh: 既又謀趨洪州，襲不可，曰：「鐘傳新興，兵附食多，未易圖也。

translations.literal: He then also planned to rush for Hongzhou; Xi objected, saying, "Zhong Chuan has just risen, his soldiers are numerous and well fed—it is not easy to scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: He next considered marching on Hongzhou, but Xi dissuaded him: "Zhong Chuan is newly ascendant, his ranks are swollen and well supplied—not an easy mark.

sentences.zh: 孫端據和州，趙暉屯上元，結此二人以圖宣州，我綽綽有餘力矣。」

translations.literal: Sun Duan holds Hezhou and Zhao Hui is stationed at Shangyuan; ally with these two to take Xuancheng, and we will have more than enough strength."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Duan holds Hezhou and Zhao Hui camps at Shangyuan—win them and strike Xuancheng, and we will have strength to spare."

sentences.zh: 行密從之。

translations.literal: Xingmi followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi took his advice.

sentences.zh: 端、暉次采石，行密自糝潭濟，端等戰不勝。

translations.literal: Duan and Hui halted at Caishi; Xingmi crossed from Santan, and Duan and the others could not win the fight.
translations.idiomatic: Duan and Hui encamped at Caishi while Xingmi crossed from Santan; they could not hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 襲勸行密「速趨曷山，堅壁以須。

translations.literal: Xi urged Xingmi, "Hurry to Mount He, hold the walls, and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Xi urged him, "March quickly to Mount He, fortify the position, and wait.

sentences.zh: 宣人求戰，示以弱，待其怠，一舉可禽」。

translations.literal: When the men of Xuancheng ask for battle, show weakness; when they grow slack, you can take them in one stroke."
translations.idiomatic: Let Xuancheng's men demand battle while you look weak; when they slacken, strike once and take them all."

sentences.zh: 宣將蘇瑭兵二萬對屯，行密不戰，分奇兵伐木開道四出，瑭驚北，遂圍宣州。

translations.literal: The Xuancheng general Su Tang encamped opposite with twenty thousand men; Xingmi would not fight, but sent flanking troops to cut timber and open paths in four directions; Tang fled north in alarm, and Xingmi then besieged Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Su Tang of Xuancheng faced him with twenty thousand men. Xingmi refused battle while detachments felled trees and opened paths on four sides. Tang fled north in panic, and Xingmi laid siege to Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 刺史趙锽糧盡，親將多出降。

translations.literal: The prefect Zhao Dui exhausted his grain, and many of his close officers came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhao Dui ran out of provisions, and many of his senior officers surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，行密有銳士五千，衣以黑繒黑甲，號「黑雲都」。

translations.literal: Earlier Xingmi had five thousand crack troops clothed in black silk and black armor, called the "Black Cloud Corps."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi had earlier raised five thousand elite troops clad in black silk and black armor, known as the Black Cloud Corps.

sentences.zh: 又並盱眙、曲溪二屯，籍其士為「黃頭軍」，以李神福為左右黃頭都尉，兵銳甚。

translations.literal: He also absorbed the garrisons at Xuyi and Quxi, enrolled their men as the "Yellow Head Army," made Li Shenfu left and right Yellow Head commandant, and the troops were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: He also absorbed the Xuyi and Quxi garrisons, enrolled their men as the Yellow Head Army, and made Li Shenfu their commander—the force was exceptionally fierce.

sentences.zh: 曲溪將劉金策锽必遁，紿曰：「將軍若出，願自吾壘而偕。」

translations.literal: The Quxi officer Liu Jin judged that Dui would surely flee and deceived him, saying, "If the general comes out, I wish to join you from my camp."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin of Quxi guessed Dui would try to escape and tricked him: "If you break out, General, I will march out from my camp and go with you."

sentences.zh: 锽喜，多遺之金，許妻以女。

translations.literal: Dui was pleased, gave him much gold, and promised his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Dui was delighted, showered him with gold, and promised him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 明日，噪城上曰：「劉郎不為爾婿！」

translations.literal: The next day he shouted from the wall, "Master Liu will not be your son-in-law!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Liu Jin shouted from the ramparts, "Master Liu is not going to be your son-in-law!"

sentences.zh: 锽宵遁，獲之。

translations.literal: Dui fled by night and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Dui slipped away by night and was captured.

sentences.zh: 锽，全忠故人也，發使求之。

translations.literal: Dui was an old acquaintance of Quanzhong, who sent envoys to request him.
translations.idiomatic: Dui was an old friend of Quanzhong's, who sent envoys asking for his safe return.

sentences.zh: 襲曰：「斬首送之，無後慮。」

translations.literal: Xi said, "Send his head and there will be no worry afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Send his head—that way there will be no trouble later."

sentences.zh: 乃歸锽首於汴。

translations.literal: He then sent Dui's head to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Dui's head to Bian.

sentences.zh: 昭宗詔行密檢校司徒、宣歙池觀察使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong appointed Xingmi acting Minister of Works and Xuancheng–She–Chi observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong named Xingmi acting Minister of Works and commissioner of the Xuancheng–She–Chi circuit.

sentences.zh: 時韓守威以功拜池州刺史，行密表徙湖州，以兵護送。

translations.literal: At the time Han Shouwei was made prefect of Chizhou for merit; Xingmi memorialized to transfer him to Huzhou and sent troops to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shouwei had just been made prefect of Chizhou for his service; Xingmi petitioned to move him to Huzhou and sent troops to escort him there.

sentences.zh: 而李師悅在湖州，與杭州刺史錢镠戰不解。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Li Shiyue was in Huzhou, fighting without end against Qian Liu, prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiyue held Huzhou and was locked in endless combat with Hangzhou prefect Qian Liu.

sentences.zh: 蘇、湖、常、潤亂甚。

translations.literal: Suzhou, Huzhou, Changzhou, and Runzhou were in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou, Huzhou, Changzhou, and Runzhou were in violent turmoil.

sentences.zh: 行密雖得宣州，而蔡儔為孫儒所破，以廬州降。

translations.literal: Although Xingmi had taken Xuancheng, Cai Chou was broken by Sun Ru and surrendered Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xingmi held Xuancheng, Cai Chou was crushed by Sun Ru and surrendered Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 儒進攻行密，行密復入揚州，北結時溥扞儒。

translations.literal: Ru pressed the attack on Xingmi; Xingmi re-entered Yangzhou and allied north with Shi Pu to resist Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Ru pressed his attack; Xingmi re-entered Yangzhou and allied north with Shi Pu to hold Ru at bay.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣龐師古將兵十萬，自潁度淮助行密，敗於高郵。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Pang Shigu with a hundred thousand troops to cross the Huai from Ying and aid Xingmi; they were defeated at Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Pang Shigu with a hundred thousand men across the Huai from Ying to aid Xingmi, but they were routed at Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 行密懼，退還宣州，遣安仁義襲成及，取潤州，自將三萬屯丹陽。

translations.literal: Xingmi was afraid, withdrew to Xuancheng, sent An Renyi to raid Cheng Ji and take Runzhou, and himself led thirty thousand to camp at Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Xingmi fell back to Xuancheng, sent An Renyi to raid Cheng Ji and seize Runzhou, and personally led thirty thousand men to camp at Danyang.

sentences.zh: 仁義又取常州，殺錢镠將杜棱。

translations.literal: Renyi also took Changzhou and killed Du Ling, a general of Qian Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi also seized Changzhou and killed Qian Liu's general Du Ling.

sentences.zh: 儒亦使劉建鋒奪潤、常。

translations.literal: Ru also sent Liu Jianfeng to seize Run and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Ru sent Liu Jianfeng to retake Runzhou and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝以杭州為防禦使，授镠；

translations.literal: The emperor made Hangzhou a defense command and invested Qian Liu;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Hangzhou a defense command and invested Qian Liu;

sentences.zh: 以宣州號寧國軍，授行密節度使。

translations.literal: and named Xuancheng the Ningguo Army, appointing Xingmi military governor.
translations.idiomatic: and named the Xuancheng command the Ningguo Army, appointing Xingmi its military governor.

sentences.zh: 大順二年，儒屯溧水，循山構壁。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dashun, Ru encamped at Lishui and built ramparts along the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In Dashun year 2, Ru encamped at Lishui and built mountain fortifications.

sentences.zh: 行密遣李神福屯廣德，計曰：「兵倍不戰，當避其銳，驕之。」

translations.literal: Xingmi sent Li Shenfu to camp at Guangde with the plan, "When the enemy doubles your numbers, do not fight; avoid their edge and make them arrogant."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Li Shenfu to Guangde with orders: "When they outnumber us, do not engage—yield their edge and let them grow arrogant."

sentences.zh: 乃退舍。

translations.literal: He then withdrew his camp.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled his camp back.

sentences.zh: 儒眾以為怯，守者懈，神福夜襲走之。

translations.literal: Ru's men thought them cowardly; the defenders slackened, and Shenfu raided by night and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's men took this for cowardice; the garrison relaxed, and Shenfu struck by night and routed them.

sentences.zh: 儒將康旺取和州，安景思取滁州。

translations.literal: Ru's generals Kang Wang took Hezhou and An Jingsi took Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's generals Kang Wang seized Hezhou and An Jingsi took Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 神福擊降旺，逐景思，攻腰山屯，破之，禽儒將李弘章。

translations.literal: Shenfu attacked, made Wang surrender, drove off Jingsi, assaulted the Yaoshan camp, broke it, and captured Ru's general Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu forced Wang to surrender, drove off Jingsi, stormed the Yaoshan camp, broke it, and captured Ru's general Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 俄而田頵、劉威為儒所敗。

translations.literal: Soon Tian Jun and Liu Wei were defeated by Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Tian Jun and Liu Wei were beaten by Ru.

sentences.zh: 行密欲守銅官，神福曰：「儒掃境以來，利速戰，宜堅壁老其師，則我無敵矣。

translations.literal: Xingmi wished to hold Tongguan; Shenfu said, "Ru has swept the region and favors swift battle—we should hold the walls and wear his army down, and then we will have no rival.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi wanted to hold Tongguan, but Shenfu said, "Ru has swept the countryside and wants a quick fight—hold the walls and wear him down, and we will be unbeatable.

sentences.zh: 又出輕騎絕賊糧道，使前不得戰，退無仰儲，不亡何待？」

translations.literal: Also send light cavalry to cut the bandits' grain routes so they cannot fight forward and have no supplies to fall back on—how can they avoid destruction?"
translations.idiomatic: Send light cavalry to cut their supply lines so they cannot advance to fight and have nothing to fall back on—how can they survive?"

sentences.zh: 於是，行密以神福為宣池都遊弈使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xingmi made Shenfu overall patrol commissioner of Xuan and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi then made Shenfu overall patrol commissioner of the Xuan–Chi region.

sentences.zh: 儒始乏食。

translations.literal: Ru began to run short of food.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's army began to run out of food.

sentences.zh: 常熟名賊陳可兒間儒、行密之鬥，竊入常州，自稱制置使。

translations.literal: Chen Ke'er, a notorious bandit of Changshu, exploited the struggle between Ru and Xingmi, slipped into Changzhou, and styled himself military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ke'er, a notorious Changshu bandit, exploited the war between Ru and Xingmi, slipped into Changzhou, and proclaimed himself military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 行密遣陶雅守潤州，張訓入揚州，因執楚州刺史，以輕兵襲常州，斬可兒。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent Tao Ya to hold Runzhou and Zhang Xun into Yangzhou; he seized the Chuzhou prefect and, with light troops, raided Changzhou and beheaded Ke'er.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Tao Ya to hold Runzhou and Zhang Xun into Yangzhou, seized the Chuzhou prefect, and with a light force raided Changzhou and killed Ke'er.

sentences.zh: 孫儒圍行密宣州，凡五月不解。

translations.literal: Sun Ru besieged Xingmi at Xuancheng for five months without lifting the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru besieged Xingmi at Xuancheng for five months without relief.

sentences.zh: 臺濛作魯陽五堰，拕輕舸饋糧，故行密軍不困，卒破儒。

translations.literal: Tai Meng built the five weirs of Luyang and towed light boats to supply grain, so Xingmi's army was not distressed and in the end broke Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Meng built the five Luyang weirs and hauled light boats to supply grain, so Xingmi's army never starved and finally broke Ru.

sentences.zh: 即表田頵守宣城，長驅入揚州。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to make Tian Jun defend Xuancheng and marched at speed into Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to leave Tian Jun in charge of Xuancheng and marched swiftly into Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 戰凡七年，定八州，生人將盡，行密勞隱休息，其下遂安。

translations.literal: The fighting lasted seven years in all; he settled eight prefectures, and the living were nearly exhausted; Xingmi comforted the weary and let them rest, and his subordinates were then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years of war had settled eight prefectures, and the population was nearly spent. Xingmi eased the burden on the people and let the land recover, and his followers found stability.

sentences.zh: 議出鹽茗畀民輸帛，幕府高勖曰：「瘡破之餘，不可以加斂。

translations.literal: They debated issuing salt and tea for the people to pay in silk; the staff member Gao Xu said, "On wounds already torn open, one cannot add levies.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed distributing salt and tea in exchange for silk payments, but staff adviser Gao Xu said, "You cannot pile levies on a land already torn open by war.

sentences.zh: 且帑貲何患不足？

translations.literal: Moreover, why worry that the treasury will not suffice?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, why worry that the treasury will run short?

sentences.zh: 若悉我所有，易四鄰所無，不積日，財有餘矣。」

translations.literal: If we trade all we have for what the four neighbors lack, in no time wealth will be in surplus."
translations.idiomatic: Trade what we have for what our neighbors lack, and in no time the treasury will overflow."

sentences.zh: 行密納之，始選吏綏勸所部。

translations.literal: Xingmi accepted this and began selecting officials to pacify and encourage his jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi accepted his counsel and began appointing officials to pacify and encourage the districts under his rule.

sentences.zh: 蔡儔以廬州叛附朱全忠，納孫儒將張顥，而倪章據舒州，與儔連和。

translations.literal: Cai Chou rebelled with Luzhou and joined Zhu Quanzhong, taking in Sun Ru's general Zhang Hao; Ni Zhang held Shuzhou and allied with Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Chou rebelled, surrendered Luzhou to Zhu Quanzhong, and took in Sun Ru's general Zhang Hao, while Ni Zhang held Shuzhou in alliance with him.

sentences.zh: 行密遣李神福攻儔，破其將，儔堅壁不出。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent Li Shenfu to attack Chou, defeated his generals, and Chou held the walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Li Shenfu against Chou, routed his generals, and Chou shut himself behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 顥超堞降，行密以隸袁積軍，積請戮之，行密愛其勇，更置於親軍。

translations.literal: Hao climbed the parapet to surrender; Xingmi placed him under Yuan Ji's army; Ji asked to execute him, but Xingmi admired his valor and reassigned him to the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hao climbed the wall to surrender. Xingmi assigned him to Yuan Ji's command; Ji asked to execute him, but Xingmi admired his courage and took him into his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，儔自殺。

translations.literal: Before long Chou killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chou took his own life.

sentences.zh: 行密先冢皆為儔發掘，吏請夷發儔世墓，不許。

translations.literal: Xingmi's ancestral tombs had all been dug up by Chou; officials asked to level Chou's family graves in return, but he would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Chou had desecrated Xingmi's ancestral graves, and officials asked to raze Chou's family tombs in revenge, but Xingmi refused.

sentences.zh: 表劉威為刺史。

translations.literal: He memorialized to make Liu Wei prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to appoint Liu Wei prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣田頵攻歙州。

translations.literal: He sent Tian Jun to attack Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tian Jun to attack Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 於是，刺史裴樞有美政，民愛之，為拒戰，頵兵數卻。

translations.literal: There the prefect Pei Shu had benevolent government and the people loved him; they fought in his defense, and Jun's troops were repeatedly driven back.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Pei Shu governed well and was beloved by the people, who fought to defend him and repeatedly drove Jun's army back.

sentences.zh: 樞，朝廷所命者，食盡欲降，遺行密書，請還京師。

translations.literal: Shu, whom the court had appointed, exhausted his provisions and wished to surrender; he sent Xingmi a letter asking to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, the court-appointed prefect, ran out of food and wished to surrender; he wrote to Xingmi asking permission to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 行密以魯郃代樞，州人不肯下，請陶雅代。

translations.literal: Xingmi replaced Shu with Lu He, but the people of the prefecture would not submit and asked that Tao Ya replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Lu He to replace Shu, but the prefecture would not submit and asked for Tao Ya instead.

sentences.zh: 雅於諸將最寬厚，以禮歸樞於朝。

translations.literal: Ya was the most generous of the generals and sent Shu back to court with full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Ya, the most magnanimous of the generals, escorted Shu back to the capital with full honors.

sentences.zh: 是歲，李神福拔舒州，倪章亡，以神福為舒州刺史。

translations.literal: That year Li Shenfu took Shuzhou; Ni Zhang fled, and Shenfu was made prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Shenfu captured Shuzhou; Ni Zhang fled, and Shenfu was appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，行密襲濠州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning, Xingmi raided Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning year 2, Xingmi raided Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 李簡重甲絕水縋而入，執刺史張遂，以劉金守之，進取壽州。

translations.literal: Li Jian, in heavy armor, crossed the water by rope, entered, seized the prefect Zhang Sui, left Liu Jin to hold it, and advanced on Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian crossed the water in heavy armor on ropes, seized Prefect Zhang Sui, left Liu Jin to hold Haozhou, and marched on Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 汴將劉知俊儲谷石碭，將南襲。

translations.literal: The Bian general Liu Zhijun stored grain at Shidang and was about to strike south.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian general Liu Zhijun stockpiled grain at Shidang and prepared to attack south.

sentences.zh: 張訓屯漣水，遣兵浮海掩得其廥。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun was stationed at Lianshui and sent troops by sea to seize his granaries by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun at Lianshui sent troops by sea and seized Zhijun's granaries in a surprise raid.

sentences.zh: 知俊戰不勝，因攻漣水，大敗，身僅免。

translations.literal: Zhijun could not win the fight and therefore attacked Lianshui, was badly defeated, and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun could not win, turned on Lianshui, suffered a crushing defeat, and barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 詔拜行密淮南節度副大使，知節度事，檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事，封弘農郡王。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xingmi deputy Huainan military commissioner, acting governor, acting Grand Tutor, and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, enfeoffing him as Prince of Hongnong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named Xingmi deputy Huainan military commissioner with full gubernatorial powers, acting Grand Tutor and Grand Councilor, and Prince of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 董昌為錢镠所攻，來告窮。

translations.literal: Dong Chang, attacked by Qian Liu, came to report his straits.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang, besieged by Qian Liu, sent word that he was at the end of his resources.

sentences.zh: 行密遣臺濛攻蘇州，安仁義、田頵攻杭州，身督戰。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent Tai Meng to attack Suzhou; An Renyi and Tian Yun attacked Hangzhou, and he personally directed the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent Tai Meng against Suzhou and An Renyi and Tian Yun against Hangzhou, taking command in person.

sentences.zh: 別將張崇為镠執，行密欲嫁其妻，答曰：「崇不負公，願少待。」

translations.literal: A separate general, Zhang Chong, was seized by Liu; Yang Xingmi wished to marry his wife; she replied: "Chong has not failed the lord — please wait a little.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Liu captured the detached commander Zhang Chong, Yang Xingmi intended to marry Chong's wife; she answered, "Chong has not betrayed you — please wait a little longer.

sentences.zh: 俄而還，自是行密終身倚愛。

translations.literal: Soon after he returned, and from then on Yang Xingmi relied on and favored her for life.
translations.idiomatic: Chong soon returned, and from that day Yang Xingmi trusted and cherished her for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，破蘇州，執镠將成及，以朱黨守之。

translations.literal: The next year in the fifth month they took Suzhou, seized Liu's general Cheng Ji, and left Zhu Dang to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the following year they captured Suzhou, took Qian Liu's general Cheng Ji prisoner, and left Zhu Dang as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 朱延壽拔蘄、光二州，行密以霍丘當南北走集，以邑豪朱景為鎮將。

translations.literal: Zhu Yanshou took Qi and Guang prefectures; as Huoqiu lay on the north-south thoroughfare, Yang Xingmi made the local magnate Zhu Jing garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanshou captured Qi and Guang; because Huoqiu stood on the main north-south route, Yang Xingmi appointed the local strongman Zhu Jing to hold it.

sentences.zh: 景驍毅絕人，諸盜莫敢犯。

translations.literal: Jing was surpassingly brave and resolute; none of the bandits dared molest him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jing was extraordinarily fierce and resolute, and no raider dared trouble his district.

sentences.zh: 汴將寇彥卿以騎三千襲之，致全忠厚意，景不許，苦戰，彥卿敗而去。

translations.literal: The Bian general Kou Yanqing raided with three thousand horse, conveying Zhu Quanzhong's sincere intent; Jing would not agree, fought bitterly, and Yanqing was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian general Kou Yanqing struck with three thousand cavalry, bearing Zhu Quanzhong's pledge of good faith; Zhu Jing refused, fought hard, and drove Yanqing off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 田頵、魏約、張宣共圍嘉興，镠大將顧全武救之，執宣、約，逐頵驛亭埭。

translations.literal: Tian Yun, Wei Yue, and Zhang Xuan jointly besieged Jiaxing; Liu's great general Gu Quanwu rescued it, seized Xuan and Yue, and drove Yun back to Yiting Dam.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yun, Wei Yue, and Zhang Xuan jointly besieged Jiaxing; Qian Liu's chief general Gu Quanwu came to the rescue, captured Xuan and Yue, and chased Tian Yun back to Yiting Dam.

sentences.zh: 未幾，泰寧節度使朱瑾率部將侯瓚來歸，太原將李承嗣、史儼、史建章亦來奔。

translations.literal: Before long, Taining military commissioner Zhu Jin came over with his subordinate general Hou Guan, and the Taiyuan generals Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and Shi Jianzhang also fled to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhu Jin, military commissioner of Taining, arrived with his officer Hou Guan; Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and Shi Jianzhang of Taiyuan also defected to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密推赤心不疑，皆以為將。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi, trusting their loyalty, made them all generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi, taking them at face value and doubting nothing, appointed them all as generals.

sentences.zh: 於是，兵銳甚，強天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon his troops were very sharp, strongest under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his army was keen-edged and unmatched in the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝惡武昌節度使杜洪與全忠合，手詔授行密江南諸道行營都統，討洪。

translations.literal: The emperor hated that Wuchang military commissioner Du Hong had joined Zhu Quanzhong; by handwritten edict he made Yang Xingmi supreme commander of the Jiangnan circuit camps to attack Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The throne resented Wuchang commissioner Du Hong's alliance with Zhu Quanzhong and by personal edict named Yang Xingmi supreme commander of the Jiangnan field armies to campaign against Hong.

sentences.zh: 汴將朱友恭、聶金率騎兵萬人與張崇戰泗州，金敗。

translations.literal: Bian generals Zhu Yougong and Nie Jin led ten thousand horsemen to fight Zhang Chong at Sizhou; Jin was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yougong and Nie Jin of Bian led ten thousand cavalry against Zhang Chong at Sizhou; Nie Jin was beaten.

sentences.zh: 瞿章守黃州，聞友恭至，南走武昌柵，行密遣將馬珣以樓船精兵助章守。

translations.literal: Qu Zhang held Huangzhou; hearing Yougong had come, he fled south to the Wuchang stockade; Yang Xingmi sent the general Ma Xun with tower ships and picked troops to help Zhang hold.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zhang defended Huangzhou; when Zhu Yougong approached he withdrew south to the Wuchang palisade, and Yang Xingmi sent Ma Xun with tower ships and elite troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 友恭次樊港，章據險，不得前，友恭鑿崖開道，以強弩叢射，殺章別將，遂圍武昌。

translations.literal: Yougong halted at Fan'gang; Zhang held the defiles and could not be approached; Yougong cut the cliffs and opened a road, raked the position with powerful crossbows, killed Zhang's lieutenant general, and then besieged Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yougong encamped at Fan'gang; Qu Zhang held the narrows and blocked him until Yougong cut a path through the cliffs, swept the heights with heavy crossbows, killed Qu Zhang's lieutenant, and invested Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 章率軍薄戰，不勝。

translations.literal: Zhang led his army in close combat and could not win.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zhang led his troops into close battle and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 友恭斬章，拔其壁。

translations.literal: Yougong beheaded Zhang and stormed his ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yougong executed Qu Zhang and overran his defenses.

sentences.zh: 全忠率葛從周萬騎攻光州，柴再用遣小校王稔以輕騎覘賊，汴兵圍之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong led Ge Congzhou with ten thousand horse to attack Guang Prefecture; Chai Zaiyong sent the junior officer Wang Min with light cavalry to reconnoiter the enemy, and Bian troops surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong led Ge Congzhou and ten thousand horsemen against Guang Prefecture; Chai Zaiyong dispatched the junior officer Wang Min with light cavalry to scout the enemy, and Bian forces surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 候者請救，再用曰：「稔必殺賊，第無往。」

translations.literal: Scouts asked for relief; Zaiyong said: "Ren is sure to kill the enemy — just do not go.
translations.idiomatic: Lookouts begged for reinforcements, but Chai Zaiyong said, "Wang Ren will certainly slaughter the enemy — stay where you are.

sentences.zh: 稔解鞍自如，暮依樾步戰，殺傷多，汴兵乃解。

translations.literal: Ren removed his saddle and acted at ease; at dusk he fought on foot among the shade trees, killing and wounding many, and the Bian troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ren unsaddled and waited calmly; at dusk he fought on foot under the trees, inflicting heavy casualties until the Bian army broke off.

sentences.zh: 時亡馬法峻，稔追汴軍，得馬乃還。

translations.literal: At the time the law on losing a horse was harsh; Ren pursued the Bian army, recovered a horse, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Horses were scarce and penalties for losing one were severe; Wang Ren chased the Bian troops, seized a mount, and only then rode back.

sentences.zh: 從周涉淮圍壽州，而龐師古、聶金以眾七萬壁清口。

translations.literal: Congzhou crossed the Huai and besieged Shouzhou, while Pang Shigu and Nie Jin encamped at Qingkou with seventy thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou crossed the Huai to besiege Shouzhou while Pang Shigu and Nie Jin walled up at Qingkou with seventy thousand men.

sentences.zh: 朱延壽擊從周軍，敗之。

translations.literal: Zhu Yanshou struck Congzhou's army and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanshou attacked Ge Congzhou's force and routed it.

sentences.zh: 行密欲汴圍解，乃擊師古。

translations.literal: Wishing to break the Bian siege, Yang Xingmi then attacked Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Intent on lifting the Bian investment, Yang Xingmi turned on Pang Shigu.

sentences.zh: 李承嗣曰：「公能潛師趨清口，破其眾，則從周不擊而潰。」

translations.literal: Li Chengsi said: "If my lord can move troops secretly toward Qingkou and rout their host, Congzhou will collapse without a blow.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengsi said, "If you can steal a march on Qingkou and smash their main force, Ge Congzhou will disintegrate without your striking him.

sentences.zh: 行密出車西門，由北門去，以銳士萬二千龁雪馳，迫清口，不進，壅淮上流灌師古軍。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi went out the carriage west gate and left by the north gate; with twelve thousand crack troops he raced through snow to Qingkou, blocked further advance, and dammed the upper Huai to flood Shigu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi rode out the carriage west gate and slipped away through the north gate; twelve thousand picked men gnawed through snow to Qingkou, halted, and dammed the upper Huai to inundate Pang Shigu's camp.

sentences.zh: 張訓自漣水來，行密使將羸兵千人為前鋒。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun came from Lianshui; Yang Xingmi had him lead a thousand weak troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun arrived from Lianshui, and Yang Xingmi sent him forward with a thousand exhausted soldiers as bait.

sentences.zh: 師古易之，方圍棋軍中，不顧。

translations.literal: Shigu held them cheap; he was playing weiqi in camp and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shigu despised them; he was playing weiqi in camp and took no notice.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾、侯瓚以百騎持汴旌幟，直入師古壘，舞槊而馳。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin and Hou Guan with a hundred horse bearing Bian banners and flags rode straight into Shigu's camp, spears dancing as they galloped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin and Hou Guan, a hundred horsemen carrying Bian standards, charged straight into Pang Shigu's lines, spears whirling.

sentences.zh: 訓亦登岸，超其柵。

translations.literal: Xun also went ashore and overleapt their palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun too came ashore and vaulted the palisade.

sentences.zh: 汴軍大囂，即斬師古，士死十八。

translations.literal: The Bian army raised a great clamor; Shigu was beheaded on the spot, and eight or nine soldiers in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian host erupted in panic; Pang Shigu was beheaded at once, and eight or nine men in ten perished.

sentences.zh: 全忠聞之，與從周皆遁走，追及壽陽，大破之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong heard of it; he and Congzhou both fled; pursued to Shouyang, they were routed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong learned the news he and Ge Congzhou fled; pursued to Shouyang, they suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 叩淠水，方涉，為瑾所乘，溺死萬餘。

translations.literal: As they knocked at the Pi River and were fording, Jin seized the moment; more than ten thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At the Pi River, as they were mid-ford, Zhu Jin struck; more than ten thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 瑾徙屯安豐，汴將牛全節苦鬥，後軍乃得度。

translations.literal: Jin moved camp to Anfeng; the Bian general Niu Quanjie fought stubbornly, and the rear guard was only then able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin shifted to Anfeng; the Bian general Niu Quanjie fought desperately until the rear guard at last got across.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，士多凍死。

translations.literal: Heavy snow came; many soldiers froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell heavily and countless men froze to death.

sentences.zh: 潁州刺史王敬蕘燎薪屬道，汴軍免者數千人。

translations.literal: Yingzhou prefect Wang Jingrao burned firewood along the road; several thousand Bian soldiers were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingrao, prefect of Yingzhou, lit bonfires all along the road, saving several thousand Bian survivors.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復圍壽州，七日走。

translations.literal: Before long they besieged Shouzhou again; after seven days they fled.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after they invested Shouzhou again, but after seven days they withdrew in flight.

sentences.zh: 馬珣收散卒三百，自黃州間道趨分寧，絕山谷，襲撫州。

translations.literal: Ma Xun gathered three hundred scattered soldiers, took a byway from Huangzhou toward Fenning, crossed mountain valleys, and raided Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun rallied three hundred stragglers, threaded a hidden route from Huangzhou to Fenning through trackless hills, and struck Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 镠將危全諷列四壁，皆萬人。

translations.literal: Liu's general Wei Quanfeng arrayed four camps, each ten thousand strong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu's general Wei Quanfeng drew up four camps, each ten thousand strong.

sentences.zh: 珣謂諸將曰：「為諸君擊中壁，食其谷以歸。」

translations.literal: Xun said to the generals: "I will strike the central camp for you; eat their grain and return.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun told his officers, "I will break the middle camp for you — eat their grain and we go home.

sentences.zh: 乃夜擊之，全諷走。

translations.literal: That night he attacked; Quanfeng fled.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked by night and Wei Quanfeng fled.

sentences.zh: 明日，珣高會，廣旗幟，伐鼓循山而下，連營潰。

translations.literal: The next day Xun held a grand feast, spread banners wide, beat drums, and came down the mountain; the linked camps collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ma Xun held a great feast, unfurled banners, beat drums, and marched down the mountain; camp after camp broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 既還，行密罵曰：「豎子，不遂據其城邪！」

translations.literal: When he returned, Yang Xingmi cursed: "You whelp — why did you not seize their city!"
translations.idiomatic: On his return Yang Xingmi berated him: "You fool — why didn't you hold the city while you had it!"

sentences.zh: 全忠攻蔡州，奉國節度使崔洪來丐師。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong attacked Caizhou; Fengguo military commissioner Cui Hong came to beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong besieged Caizhou, and Fengguo commissioner Cui Hong came pleading for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣朱瑾率兵萬人攻徐州，屯呂梁，洪遂來奔。

translations.literal: The next year he sent Zhu Jin with ten thousand men to attack Xuzhou, encamped at Lüliang, and Hong then came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yang Xingmi sent Zhu Jin with ten thousand men against Xuzhou, encamped at Lüliang, and Cui Hong defected to his side.

sentences.zh: 會雨霖，瑾引還。

translations.literal: Continuous rains came; Jin withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Relentless rains set in and Zhu Jin pulled back.

sentences.zh: 行密攻徐州，汴將李禮壁宿州以援，全忠自將次輝州。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi attacked Xuzhou; the Bian general Li Li walled up Suzhou in relief; Zhu Quanzhong personally led troops and halted at Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi assaulted Xuzhou; the Bian general Li Li fortified Suzhou in support while Zhu Quanzhong himself advanced and stopped at Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 行密戰不勝，乃解。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi could not win the fight and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi failed to prevail and broke off the siege.

sentences.zh: 青州將陳漢賓擁兵送款行密，王綰、張訓、周本率兵迎之，漢賓中悔，綰、訓入見漢賓，約麾下：「饗我不過日中，若不至，可攻城。」

translations.literal: Qingzhou general Chen Hanbin came with troops to offer allegiance to Yang Xingmi; Wang Wan, Zhang Xun, and Zhou Ben led troops to welcome him; Hanbin halfway repented; Wan and Xun entered to see Hanbin and told his followers: "Entertain us no later than noon — if you do not come, you may storm the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hanbin of Qingzhou marched over to submit to Yang Xingmi; Wang Wan, Zhang Xun, and Zhou Ben went out to receive him; Hanbin wavered midway; Wan and Xun entered to see him and warned his men, "Feast us by noon — if you do not, we storm the walls.

sentences.zh: 漢賓釋甲聽命。

translations.literal: Hanbin removed his armor and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hanbin laid down his arms and submitted.

sentences.zh: 光州叛，行密自攻之，汴將朱友裕來救，撤圍還。

translations.literal: Guang Prefecture rebelled; Yang Xingmi attacked it himself; the Bian general Zhu Youyu came to rescue it; he raised the siege and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Prefecture revolted; Yang Xingmi led the assault in person until Zhu Youyu of Bian came to its relief, whereupon he lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 全忠諭馬殷、成汭、雷滿合兵攻行密，汭、滿猶豫，汭惡殷事全忠，掠其境，滿來結好。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong urged Ma Yin, Cheng Ru, and Lei Man to join forces against Yang Xingmi; Ru and Man hesitated; Ru hated that Yin served Zhu Quanzhong and raided his territory; Man came to make friendly ties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong pressed Ma Yin, Cheng Ru, and Lei Man to unite against Yang Xingmi; Ru and Man hung back; Ru resented Yin's ties to Zhu Quanzhong and raided his lands, while Man sought friendship with Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密壁黃、鄂間，杜洪寘鴆於酒、於井，棄城去，行密知，不入。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi entrenched between Huang and E; Du Hong put poison in wine and in wells and abandoned the city; Yang Xingmi knew and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi camped between Huang and E; Du Hong laced wine and wells with poison and fled the city; Yang Xingmi, warned, would not enter.

sentences.zh: 全忠又遣使者督殷、汭、滿連兵解圍，行密還。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong again sent envoys to urge Yin, Ru, and Man to unite their armies and raise the siege; Yang Xingmi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong again dispatched envoys to drive Yin, Ru, and Man into combined action and lift the siege; Yang Xingmi pulled back.

sentences.zh: 詔加檢校太尉、兼侍中。

translations.literal: An edict added to his titles Acting Grand Marshal and Vice Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to Acting Grand Marshal and Vice Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 天復元年，傳言盜殺錢镠，李神福急攻臨安，顧全武列八壁相望，神福伏軍青山，偽若引去，諜奔告，全武悉眾躡之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianfu, rumor spread that bandits had killed Qian Liu; Li Shenfu pressed the attack on Lin'an; Gu Quanwu arrayed eight camps facing one another; Shenfu hid troops at Qingshan and feigned withdrawal; spies ran to report; Quanwu led his entire force in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianfu rumor said bandits had killed Qian Liu; Li Shenfu pressed hard on Lin'an; Gu Quanwu drew eight camps in a chain; Shenfu hid men at Qingshan and pretended to retreat; spies raced to report, and Gu Quanwu marched out in full pursuit.

sentences.zh: 神福返鬥，與伏夾攻，斬首五千級，執全武。

translations.literal: Shenfu turned and fought; with the ambush he attacked from both sides, beheaded five thousand, and seized Quanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu wheeled and fought; ambush and main body struck together, taking five thousand heads and capturing Gu Quanwu.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂圍臨安，镠將秦昶以步兵三千降。

translations.literal: The next day he besieged Lin'an; Liu's general Qin Chang surrendered with three thousand foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he invested Lin'an; Qian Liu's general Qin Chang surrendered with three thousand infantry.

sentences.zh: 神福乃令軍中護镠先墓，禁樵采，镠遣使者厚謝。

translations.literal: Shenfu then ordered the army to protect Liu's ancestral graves and forbid woodcutting; Liu sent envoys with deep thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu then posted guards at Qian Liu's ancestral tombs and forbade logging; Qian Liu sent envoys with lavish thanks.

sentences.zh: 神福以镠不死，臨安未可下，納犒而還。

translations.literal: Shenfu, knowing Liu was not dead and Lin'an could not be taken, accepted rewards and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu, seeing that Qian Liu lived and Lin'an would not fall, accepted tribute and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，大將劉存率兵二萬、戰艫七百伐湖南。

translations.literal: The next year the great general Liu Cun led twenty thousand troops and seven hundred warships to attack Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the chief general Liu Cun sailed against Hunan with twenty thousand men and seven hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 殷伏軍長磧洲，以樓艓據上流，乘風飏沙，強弩射之，存軍。

translations.literal: Yin lay in ambush at Changqi Shoal, positioned tower ships upstream, raised sand on the wind, and shot with powerful crossbows; Liu Cun's army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin ambushed him at Changqi Shoal, blocked the upstream with tower ships, whipped sand into the air on the wind, and raked the fleet with heavy crossbows until Liu Cun's army was broken and driven off.

sentences.zh: 行密歸顧全武於镠，镠亦釋秦裴以報。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi returned Gu Quanwu to Liu; Liu also released Qin Pei in return.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent Gu Quanwu back to Qian Liu, who in turn released Qin Pei as a reciprocal gesture.

sentences.zh: 帝在鳳翔，以左金吾大將軍李儼為江淮宣諭使，授行密東面諸道行營都統、檢校太師、守中書令，封吳王，承制封拜，且告難。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Fengxiang; he made Left Golden Guard grand general Li Yan envoy to proclaim and soothe the Jiang-Huai region, granting Yang Xingmi supreme commander of the eastern circuit camps, Acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian of the Secretariat Director, enfeoffment as Prince of Wu, authority to appoint by imperial mandate, and also reporting the court's distress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Fengxiang; he named Left Golden Guard grand general Li Yan envoy to the Jiang-Huai, invested Yang Xingmi as supreme commander of the eastern circuits, Acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Wu, with power to appoint officials by imperial writ, and sent word of the throne's peril.

sentences.zh: 時已削奪全忠封爵，詔西川、河東、忠義、幽州、保大、橫海、義武、大同八道攻之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Quanzhong's rank and fief had already been stripped; an edict ordered the eight circuits of Xichuan, Hedong, Zhongyi, Youzhou, Baoda, Henghai, Yiwu, and Datong to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong's titles had already been revoked; an edict commanded eight circuits — Xichuan, Hedong, Zhongyi, Youzhou, Baoda, Henghai, Yiwu, and Datong — to move against him.

sentences.zh: 詔朱瑾為平盧節度使，繇海州取青、齊；

translations.literal: Zhu Jin was ordered made Pinglu military commissioner, to take Qing and Qi via Haizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin was commissioned Pinglu military commissioner, to seize Qing and Qi by way of Haizhou;

sentences.zh: 馮弘鐸為感化節度使，出漣水，攻徐、宿；

translations.literal: Feng Hongduo was made Ganhuo military commissioner, to issue from Lianshui and attack Xu and Su;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hongduo was made Ganhuo military commissioner, to advance from Lianshui against Xu and Su;

sentences.zh: 使朱延壽圍蔡州；

translations.literal: Zhu Yanshou was to besiege Caizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanshou was to invest Caizhou;

sentences.zh: 田頵捍錢勖；

translations.literal: Tian Yun was to hold off Qian Liu;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yun was to contain Qian Liu;

sentences.zh: 行密討杜洪、馬殷，以分全忠勢。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi was to attack Du Hong and Ma Yin to divide Zhu Quanzhong's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi was to strike Du Hong and Ma Yin and so split Zhu Quanzhong's power.

sentences.zh: 行密乃以李神福為鄂嶽招討使，劉存副之，遣冷業攻馬殷。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi then made Li Shenfu commissioner for recruiting and suppressing E and Yue, with Liu Cun as his deputy, and sent Leng Ye to attack Ma Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi appointed Li Shenfu commissioner for the E-Yue campaign with Liu Cun as deputy, and dispatched Leng Ye against Ma Yin.

sentences.zh: 杜洪戰屢敗，嬰城，請救於全忠。

translations.literal: Du Hong was repeatedly defeated in battle, clung to the city, and begged Zhu Quanzhong for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong lost battle after battle, shut himself in the city, and pleaded to Zhu Quanzhong for aid.

sentences.zh: 全忠使韓率步兵萬人屯灄口，荊南節度使成汭亦悉眾救洪。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent Han Qing to lead ten thousand foot soldiers to encamp at Zhuankou; Jingnan military commissioner Cheng Ru also brought his entire force to rescue Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Han Qing with ten thousand infantry to Zhuankou, and Jingnan commissioner Cheng Ru marched out in full strength to relieve Hong.

sentences.zh: 神福逆戰，敗之，汭溺死，引眾走。

translations.literal: Shenfu met them in battle, defeated them; Ru drowned; the rest fled with their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu met them head-on, broke them, and Cheng Ru drowned; the survivors fled.

sentences.zh: 冷業屯平江，為三壁。

translations.literal: Leng Ye encamped at Pingjiang in three camps.
translations.idiomatic: Leng Ye walled up at Pingjiang in three positions.

sentences.zh: 殷將許德勛以銳卒號「定南刀」夜襲業，擊三壁皆破，禽業，掠上高、唐年而去。

translations.literal: Yin's general Xu Dexun with crack troops called "South-Pacifying Blades" raided Ye by night, broke all three camps, captured Ye, and plundered Shanggao and Tangnian before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin's general Xu Dexun, leading elite troops nicknamed the South-Pacifying Blades, struck by night, overran all three camps, took Leng Ye prisoner, and withdrew after sacking Shanggao and Tangnian.

sentences.zh: 是時，杜洪困甚，且禽；

translations.literal: At this time Du Hong was in extreme straits and was about to be captured;
translations.idiomatic: By then Du Hong was desperate and on the verge of capture;

sentences.zh: 會田頵、安仁義絕行密，行密召神福、存還計事，洪復振。

translations.literal: but Tian Yun and An Renyi broke with Yang Xingmi; Yang Xingmi recalled Shenfu and Cun to consult on the matter, and Hong revived.
translations.idiomatic: but Tian Yun and An Renyi rebelled against Yang Xingmi; he recalled Li Shenfu and Liu Cun to deal with the crisis, and Du Hong rallied.

sentences.zh: 頵之敗，更以臺濛為宣州觀察使，復遣神福、存攻鄂州。

translations.literal: After Yun's defeat, Tai Meng was again made Xuanczhou observation commissioner, and Shenfu and Cun were again sent to attack Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Tian Yun's defeat Yang Xingmi reappointed Tai Meng Xuanczhou observation commissioner and again sent Li Shenfu and Liu Cun against Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 順義軍使汪武與頵連和，歙州刺史陶雅攻鐘傳，兵過武所，迎謁，縛武於軍。

translations.literal: Shunyi army commissioner Wang Wu joined with Yun; Shezhou prefect Tao Ya attacked Zhong Chuan; when his troops passed Wu's post, Wu came out to welcome him and was bound in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shunyi army commissioner Wang Wu had allied with Tian Yun; when Shezhou prefect Tao Ya marched against Zhong Chuan and passed Wu's station, Wu came out to greet him and was seized in camp.

sentences.zh: 無錫當浙沖，行密使票將張可悰守之。

translations.literal: Wuxi lay on the Zhejiang thoroughfare; Yang Xingmi sent adjutant general Zhang Keyong to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxi guarded the Zhejiang corridor; Yang Xingmi posted adjutant general Zhang Keyong there.

sentences.zh: 镠勁兵三千夜襲城，可悰以百騎擊走之，吏皆賀，答曰：「未也，方勞諸軍一戰。」

translations.literal: Liu sent three thousand crack troops to raid the city by night; Keyong drove them off with a hundred horse; the officers all congratulated him; he replied: "Not yet — I mean to ask the army for one more fight.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent three thousand picked men in a night assault; Zhang Keyong repulsed them with a hundred horsemen; his staff congratulated him, but he said, "Not yet — I mean to give the men one more battle.

sentences.zh: 乃蔽火斂旗以須。

translations.literal: He then hid the fires and furled the banners to wait.
translations.idiomatic: He doused the watchfires, furled the banners, and waited.

sentences.zh: 覘者以告，镠兵復至，可悰大破之。

translations.literal: Scouts reported it; Liu's troops came again; Keyong routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When scouts brought word that Qian Liu's men were returning, Zhang Keyong crushed them completely.

sentences.zh: 臺濛卒，行密以子渥為宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: Tai Meng died; Yang Xingmi made his son Wo Xuanczhou observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai Meng died, Yang Xingmi appointed his son Yang Wo Xuanczhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年，王茂章、李德誠拔潤州，殺安仁義。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianyou, Wang Maozhang and Li Decheng took Runzhou and killed An Renyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou year 2, Wang Maozhang and Li Decheng captured Runzhou and killed An Renyi.

sentences.zh: 以王茂章為潤州團練使。

translations.literal: Wang Maozhang was made Runzhou regimental commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhang was appointed Runzhou regimental commissioner.

sentences.zh: 聶彥章等率舟師復伐殷，攻岳州。

translations.literal: Nie Yanzhang and others led a fleet again to attack Yin and assault Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Yanzhang and others led the river force against Ma Yin once more, attacking Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 許德勛、詹佶以舟千二百柁入蛤子湖棄山之南，為木龍鎖舟，夜徙三百舸斷楊林岸。

translations.literal: Xu Dexun and Zhan Ji entered Gazihu south of Qishan with twelve hundred hulls, made wooden dragons to chain the boats, and by night moved three hundred vessels to cut the Yanglin shore.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dexun and Zhan Ji brought twelve hundred hulls into Gazihu south of Qishan, linked the fleet with chained wooden dragons, and under cover of night shifted three hundred boats to sever the Yanglin bank.

sentences.zh: 彥章入荊江，將趨江陵。

translations.literal: Yanzhang entered the Jing River and was about to hasten toward Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang entered the Jing River and was pressing toward Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 佶躡之，德勛以梅花海鶻迅舸進，斷木龍，舟蔽江，車弩亂發，執彥章，溺死萬人。

translations.literal: Ji pursued him; Dexun advanced with swift Meihua Haihe boats, severed the wooden dragons, boats covered the river, chariot crossbows fired in confusion, captured Yanzhang, and ten thousand men drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Ji pursued him; Dexun drove forward in swift Meihua Haihe boats, cut the chained wooden dragons, filled the river with hulls, and unleashed chariot crossbows in wild volleys until Yanzhang was taken and ten thousand men drowned.

sentences.zh: 殷釋彥章還，德勛謂曰：「為我謝吳王，仆等數人在，湖、湘不可冀也。」

translations.literal: Yin released Yanzhang to return; Dexun said to him: "Convey my thanks to the Prince of Wu—we few remain, and the lakes and Xiang region cannot be hoped for."
translations.idiomatic: Yin released Yanzhang to go home; Dexun told him, "Give my thanks to the Prince of Wu: so long as we few are here, there is no hope for the lake country or Hunan."

sentences.zh: 行密寬易，善遇下，能得士死力。

translations.literal: Xingmi was generous and easygoing, treated subordinates well, and could win men to fight to the death for him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was open-handed and even-tempered, treated his men well, and could win them to die for him.

sentences.zh: 每宴，使人負劍侍。

translations.literal: At every banquet he had men carry swords and attend him.
translations.idiomatic: At every feast he had sword-bearers stand at his side.

sentences.zh: 陳人張洪因以劍擊行密，不中，近將李龍禽斬之。

translations.literal: A man of Chen, Zhang Hong, took this occasion to strike at Xingmi with a sword but missed; the attendant general Li Longqin cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong of Chen seized the moment to slash at Xingmi with a sword and missed; the attendant general Li Longqin struck him down.

sentences.zh: 佗日，侍劍如故。

translations.literal: Another day, sword-bearing attendants served as before.
translations.idiomatic: On another day the sword-bearers attended him just as before.

sentences.zh: 行密蚤出，有盜斷馬鞅，不之問，以故人人懷恩。

translations.literal: Xingmi went out early one morning and a thief cut his horse's girth; he did not investigate the matter, and for this reason everyone cherished his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xingmi went out early and a thief cut his horse's girth; he asked no questions about it, and for that reason every man felt bound to him.

sentences.zh: 始，乘孫儒亂，府庫殫空，能約己省費，不三年而軍富雄。

translations.literal: At the start, taking advantage of Sun Ru's turmoil, the treasury was utterly empty; he could restrain himself and cut expenses, and in less than three years the army grew rich and strong.
translations.idiomatic: At first, amid Sun Ru's chaos, the treasury was bare; by restraining himself and cutting costs, he made the army rich and formidable in less than three years.

sentences.zh: 嘗過楚州，臺濛盛供帳待之，行密一夕去，遺衣臥內，皆經補浣。

translations.literal: Once passing through Chuzhou, Tai Meng laid out lavish provisions to receive him; Xingmi left after one night, leaving behind clothes in the bedchamber—all patched and washed.
translations.idiomatic: Once, passing through Chuzhou, Tai Meng laid out a lavish reception; Xingmi stayed only one night and left behind clothes in the bedchamber—all patched and washed.

sentences.zh: 濛還之，行密曰：「吾興細微，不敢忘本，君笑我邪？」

translations.literal: Meng returned them; Xingmi said, "I rose from humble beginnings and dare not forget my roots—are you laughing at me?
translations.idiomatic: Meng sent the clothes back; Xingmi said, "I rose from nothing and dare not forget where I came from—are you mocking me?

sentences.zh: 濛大慚。

translations.literal: Meng was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 登城，見王茂章營第，曰：「天下未定，而茂章居寢郁然，渠肯為我忘身乎？」

translations.literal: Ascending the wall, he saw Wang Maozhang's commodious residence and said, "The realm is not yet settled, yet Maozhang dwells in such lush comfort—will he truly forget himself and die for me?
translations.idiomatic: From the wall he saw Wang Maozhang's spacious quarters and said, "The empire is still unsettled, yet Maozhang lives in such ease—will he ever forget himself and die for me?

sentences.zh: 茂章遽毀損。

translations.literal: Maozhang hurriedly had it demolished and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang at once had it torn down and scaled back.

sentences.zh: 方帝困鳳翔，再遣使督兵，以為行密可亢全忠者，然兵至宿州，紿言糧盡，乃還。

translations.literal: Just then the Emperor was besieged at Fengxiang; twice he sent envoys to press troops forward, thinking Xingmi could stand against Quanzhong; yet when the army reached Suzhou, they falsely claimed provisions were exhausted and returned.
translations.idiomatic: While the Emperor was trapped at Fengxiang, the court twice sent envoys to urge Xingmi's army forward, counting on him to check Quanzhong; but when the troops reached Suzhou they falsely claimed their grain was gone and turned back.

sentences.zh: 全忠脅帝東遷，行密恥憤被病。

translations.literal: Quanzhong coerced the Emperor to move east; Xingmi, shamed and enraged, fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong forced the Emperor to move east; Xingmi, shamed and furious, took to his bed.

sentences.zh: 全忠亦知天子倚行密為重，乃弒帝以絕人望。

translations.literal: Quanzhong also knew the Son of Heaven relied on Xingmi as a counterweight, and so he assassinated the Emperor to cut off people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong also knew the throne leaned on Xingmi as a counterweight, and so he murdered the Emperor to break the world's hope.

sentences.zh: 行密聞之，發喪，不視事三日，因是病篤，召將吏付家事，問嗣於其佐。

translations.literal: When Xingmi heard this, he observed mourning, did not attend to affairs for three days, and because of this his illness grew grave; he summoned generals and officials to entrust his household affairs and asked his aides about succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi heard the news, he went into mourning and set aside business for three days; his illness then worsened, and he summoned his officers, settled his household affairs, and asked his advisers whom to name as heir.

sentences.zh: 周隱對曰：「宣州司徒易而信讒，唯淫酗是好，不可以嗣，不如擇賢者。」

translations.literal: Zhou Yin replied: "The Steward of Xuancheng, Wo, is simple-minded and believes slander; he delights only in lechery and drink—he cannot succeed; better to choose a worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yin answered, "The Xuancheng steward Wo is simple and credulous of slander, cares for nothing but wine and women, and cannot succeed you; better to choose a worthy man.

sentences.zh: 時劉威以宿將有威名，隱意屬威，行密不答。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Wei, an old general with a commanding reputation, was whom Yin intended; Xingmi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei, an old commander of great standing, was the man Yin had in mind; Xingmi made no reply.

sentences.zh: 因以王茂章代渥，使亟還。

translations.literal: He then had Wang Maozhang replace Wo and ordered him to return at once.
translations.idiomatic: He then put Wang Maozhang in Wo's place and ordered him to return at once.

sentences.zh: 行密召所親嚴求曰：「我使周隱召吾兒而不至，奈何？」

translations.literal: Xingmi summoned his close follower Yan Qiu and said, "I sent Zhou Yin to summon my son, yet he has not come—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi called his confidant Yan Qiu and said, "I sent Zhou Yin to summon my son, and he has not come—what can be done?

sentences.zh: 求往見隱，召檄仍在幾。

translations.literal: Qiu went to see Yin; the summons document still lay on the desk.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu went to see Yin and found the summons still lying on his desk.

sentences.zh: 始，渥守宣州，押牙徐溫、王令謀約渥曰：「王且疾，而君出外，此殆奸人計。

translations.literal: At the start, when Wo was holding Xuancheng, the ya-ya officers Xu Wen and Wang Ling secretly agreed with Wo and said, "The Prince is ill, yet you are sent abroad—this is likely a schemer's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Wo held Xuancheng, the staff officers Xu Wen and Wang Ling secretly warned him, "The Prince is ill and you have been sent away—this is probably someone's plot.

sentences.zh: 他日有召，非我二人勿應也。」

translations.literal: If you are summoned another day, respond to no one but the two of us.
translations.idiomatic: If you are summoned later, answer to no one but the two of us.

sentences.zh: 及是，二人以符召渥。

translations.literal: At this juncture the two men summoned Wo with the tally.
translations.idiomatic: When the moment came, the two men summoned Wo with the command tally.

sentences.zh: 渥至，行密承制授檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事、淮南節度使留後。

translations.literal: When Wo arrived, Xingmi received imperial writ and appointed him honorary Grand General, co-equal Director of the Chancellery, and acting Huainan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo arrived, Xingmi received imperial authorization and appointed him honorary Grand General, co-equal Director of the Chancellery, and acting Huainan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 行密諗渥曰：「左衙都將張顥、王茂章、李遇皆怙亂，不得為兒除之。」

translations.literal: Xingmi told Wo: "The left-gate commanders Zhang Hao, Wang Maozhang, and Li Yu all rely on disorder—you cannot remove them for my son.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi warned Wo, "The left-gate commanders Zhang Hao, Wang Maozhang, and Li Yu all thrive on chaos—you cannot remove them for my son's sake.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 遺令谷葛為衣，桐瓦為棺。

translations.literal: His dying order was: grain-sack cloth for garments, paulownia tiles for a coffin.
translations.idiomatic: His last instructions were to be buried in coarse sackcloth and a coffin of paulownia tiles.

sentences.zh: 夜葬山谷，人不知所在。

translations.literal: He was buried by night in a mountain valley; no one knew where.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried by night in a mountain valley, and no one knew the place.

sentences.zh: 諸將謚曰武忠。

translations.literal: The generals gave him the posthumous title Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The generals gave him the posthumous title Martial and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 張顥議歸都統印於宣諭使李儼，行節度事。

translations.literal: Zhang Hao proposed returning the commander's seal to the Imperial Emissary Li Yan and exercising military affairs himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao proposed surrendering the commander's seal to the imperial emissary Li Yan and running military affairs himself.

sentences.zh: 諸將畏顥，無敢對，渥流涕。

translations.literal: The generals feared Hao and none dared reply; Wo wept.
translations.idiomatic: The generals feared Hao and no one dared answer; Wo wept.

sentences.zh: 騎軍都尉李濤曰：「都統印，先帝所以賜王父子，安得授人？」

translations.literal: Cavalry commander Li Tao said, "The commander's seal was bestowed by the late Emperor upon the Prince and his son—how can it be handed to another?
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry commander Li Tao said, "The commander's seal was given by the late Emperor to the Prince and his son—how can it be handed to anyone else?

sentences.zh: 諸將唯唯。

translations.literal: The generals murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: The generals murmured agreement.

sentences.zh: 顥投袂去，乃共請於儼，承制授渥兼侍中、淮南節度副大使、東面諸道行營都統，封弘農郡王。

translations.literal: Hao flung his sleeve and left; they then jointly petitioned Yan, and by imperial writ Wo was appointed concurrent Palace Attendant, Huainan deputy military commissioner, Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Circuit Armies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Hongnong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hao flung his sleeve and stalked off; the others then petitioned Yan together, and by imperial writ Wo was made concurrent Palace Attendant, Huainan deputy military commissioner, commander-in-chief of the eastern circuits, and Prince of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 渥好騎射。

translations.literal: Wo loved horseback riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Wo loved riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 初與許玄膺為刎頸交，及嗣位，事皆決之，諸將莫敢忤。

translations.literal: At first he and Xu Xuanying were sworn friends unto death; once he succeeded, all affairs were decided by Xu, and no general dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xu Xuanying had been sworn friends unto death; once Wo succeeded, Xu decided every matter, and no general dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 渥求王茂章親兵不得，及去宣，輦帷帟以行，茂章嫚罵不與。

translations.literal: Wo sought Wang Maozhang's personal troops but could not obtain them; when he left Xuancheng he had curtains and canopies carted along, and Maozhang reviled him and would not yield them.
translations.idiomatic: Wo asked Wang Maozhang for his personal guard and was refused; when he left Xuancheng he had curtains and canopies carted away, and Maozhang cursed him and would not give them up.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遣兵五千襲之，茂章奔杭州。

translations.literal: After a year he sent five thousand troops to attack him; Maozhang fled to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he sent five thousand men against him; Maozhang fled to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦裴執鐘匡時，渥授以江西制置使。

translations.literal: Qin Pei captured Zhong Kuangshi; Wo appointed him Jiangxi frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Pei captured Zhong Kuangshi, and Wo made him Jiangxi frontier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朱思、範師從、陳潘以兵戍洪州，渥為張顥所制，三人者，渥腹心也。

translations.literal: Zhu Si, Fan Shicong, and Chen Pan garrisoned Hongzhou with troops; Wo was controlled by Zhang Hao—the three men were Wo's trusted confidants.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Si, Fan Shicong, and Chen Pan held Hongzhou with troops; Wo was under Zhang Hao's thumb, and the three were his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 顥脅以為有異謀，遣陳祐疾馳，懷短兵，微服入秦裴帳中，裴大驚，命飲，召三將入，皆色動，酒行，祐數其罪，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Hao coerced Qin Pei with accusations of subversive plotting, sent Chen You galloping in haste, bearing short weapons, entering Qin Pei's tent in disguise; Pei was greatly alarmed, ordered wine served, summoned the three generals in—they all changed color; as the wine circulated, You enumerated their crimes and all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Hao framed Qin Pei for treason and sent Chen You galloping ahead with concealed blades; Chen entered Pei's tent in disguise. Pei was startled, ordered wine, and summoned the three generals—they all paled. As the cups went round, Chen listed their crimes and had them all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 渥召周隱曰：「君嘗以孤為不可嗣，何也？」

translations.literal: Wo summoned Zhou Yin and said, "You once held that I was unfit to succeed—why?
translations.idiomatic: Wo summoned Zhou Yin and said, "You once said I was unfit to succeed—why?

sentences.zh: 隱不對，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Yin did not answer, and Wo had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin made no answer, and Wo had him killed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：行密興賤微，及得誌，仁恕善禦眾，治身節儉，無大過失，可謂賢矣。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: Xingmi rose from low estate; once he achieved his aim, he was benevolent and forgiving, skilled at commanding the multitude, frugal in personal conduct, without grave faults—he may be called worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Xingmi rose from humble origins; once he had his wish, he was humane and forgiving, skilled at holding men together, frugal in his own life, and without grave fault—he may be called worthy.

sentences.zh: 然所據淮、楚，士氣剽而不剛。

translations.literal: Yet the region he held, Huai and Chu, had troops spirited but not steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Huai and Chu country he held produced soldiers fierce but not resolute.

sentences.zh: 行密無霸材，不能提兵為四方倡，以興王室，熟視朱溫劫天子而東，謀窮意沮，憤死牖下，可為長太息矣！

translations.literal: Xingmi lacked the talent for hegemony; he could not raise armies to lead the four quarters and revive the royal house, but watched Zhu Wen carry off the Son of Heaven eastward—plans exhausted, will broken, he died in rage beneath his window; one may deeply sigh over this!
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi lacked the stuff of a hegemon; he could not take up arms to lead the realm and restore the throne, but watched Zhu Wen carry the Son of Heaven east—his plans spent, his spirit broken, he died in rage at his window. One can only sigh long over it.

sentences.zh: 時溥，徐州彭城人。

translations.literal: Shi Pu was a native of Pengcheng in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu came from Pengcheng in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 為州牙將。

translations.literal: He served as a ya general of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a staff general of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 黃巢亂京師，節度使支詳遣溥與陳璠率兵五千西討。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao threw the capital into turmoil, military commissioner Zhi Xiang sent Pu and Chen Fan to lead five thousand troops west to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao threw the capital into chaos, military commissioner Zhi Xiang sent Pu and Chen Fan west with five thousand men to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 次河陰，軍亂，剽居人。

translations.literal: When they reached Heyin, the army mutinied and plundered the inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin the army mutinied and looted the townspeople.

sentences.zh: 溥招戢其眾，引還屯境上，疑不敢歸。

translations.literal: Pu gathered and pacified the troops, withdrew and encamped on the border, fearful and not daring to return.
translations.idiomatic: Pu rallied the men, withdrew, and encamped on the frontier, afraid to go home.

sentences.zh: 詳以牛酒犒士，約悉貰其罪，軍乃入，共推溥為留後，逐詳客館。

translations.literal: Xiang rewarded the men with cattle and wine, promising to pardon all their crimes; the army then entered, jointly acclaimed Pu as acting commissioner, and drove Xiang out to lodge at an inn.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang sent cattle and wine to reward the troops and promised to pardon all their crimes; the army then marched in, acclaimed Pu acting commissioner, and drove Xiang out to a guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 溥厚具貲裝，遣璠護還京師，夜駐七里亭，璠擅殺詳，屠其家。

translations.literal: Pu amply furnished travel goods and sent Fan to escort Xiang back to the capital; at night they halted at Qili Pavilion, and Fan on his own authority killed Xiang and slaughtered his household.
translations.idiomatic: Pu richly equipped Xiang for the road and sent Fan to escort him to the capital; that night at Qili Pavilion Fan killed Xiang on his own authority and slaughtered his household.

sentences.zh: 溥怒，署璠宿州刺史，俄殺之。

translations.literal: Pu was enraged; he appointed Fan prefect of Suzhou, then soon had him killed.
