translations.idiomatic: Pu was furious; he appointed Fan prefect of Suzhou and soon had him killed.

sentences.zh: 別遣將引銳兵三千入關，僖宗因以武寧節度命之。

translations.literal: Separately he sent a general leading three thousand crack troops into the passes; Emperor Xizong thereupon appointed him Wuning military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a general with three thousand picked troops through the passes, and Emperor Xizong thereupon made him Wuning military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 巢敗東走，圍陳州，營溵水。

translations.literal: When Chao was defeated and fled east, he besieged Chenzhou and encamped on the Yin River.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao was beaten and fled east, he besieged Chenzhou and encamped on the Yin River.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權方據淮西，相聯結。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan then held Huaidong and they joined forces.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan then held the Huai west and the two joined forces.

sentences.zh: 溥地介於賊，乃悉師討之，軍鋒甚盛，連戰輒克，授東面兵馬都統。

translations.literal: Pu's territory lay between the bandits, so he marched the whole force against them; his army's edge was very keen, battle after battle he prevailed, and he was appointed Commander of Eastern Armies and Horses.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's land lay between the rebels, so he marched his whole force against them; his army's edge was sharp, he won battle after battle, and was made commander of the eastern armies and horses.

sentences.zh: 遂合許、兗、鄆兵，逐尚讓於太康，斬首數萬級，讓以所部萬人降。

translations.literal: He then combined troops from Xu, Yan, and Yun, drove Shang Rang at Taikang, beheaded tens of thousands, and Rang surrendered with ten thousand men under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He then combined the armies of Xu, Yan, and Yun, routed Shang Rang at Taikang, took tens of thousands of heads, and Rang surrendered with ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 溥遣將李師悅等追尾巢至萊蕪，大破之。

translations.literal: Pu sent generals Li Shiyue and others to pursue Chao's tail to Laiwu and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Pu sent Li Shiyue and others to pursue Chao's rear guard to Laiwu and broke him completely.

sentences.zh: 諸將爭得巢首，而林言斬之，持歸溥，以獻天子，故破賊溥功第一。

translations.literal: Generals contended to seize Chao's head, but Lin Yan beheaded him and brought it back to Pu, presenting it to the Son of Heaven; thus in destroying the bandits Pu's merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Generals fought over who would take Chao's head, but Lin Yan cut it off and brought it to Pu, who presented it to the throne; in crushing the rebels Pu's merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 加檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事，進檢校太尉、兼中書令、鉅鹿郡王。

translations.literal: He was promoted to honorary Minister of Works and co-equal Director of the Chancellery, then advanced to honorary Grand General, concurrent Central Secretariat Director, and Prince of Julu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made honorary Minister of Works and co-equal Director of the Chancellery, then promoted to honorary Grand General, concurrent Central Secretariat Director, and Prince of Julu.

sentences.zh: 宗權阻兵，拜溥蔡州行營兵馬都統。

translations.literal: Zongquan obstructed with arms; Pu was appointed Commander of Caizhou Field Armies and Horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongquan took up arms in obstruction, Pu was appointed commander of the Caizhou field armies and horses.

sentences.zh: 賊平，與朱全忠爭功，嫌惎日構。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he and Zhu Quanzhong disputed merit; mutual resentment grew day by day.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, he and Zhu Quanzhong quarreled over credit, and mutual hatred grew by the day.

sentences.zh: 孫儒方與楊行密爭揚州，詔全忠為淮南節度使平其亂。

translations.literal: Sun Ru was then contending with Yang Xingmi for Yangzhou; an edict made Quanzhong Huainan military commissioner to quell the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru was then fighting Yang Xingmi for Yangzhou, and an edict made Quanzhong Huainan military commissioner to put down the disorder.

sentences.zh: 溥自以先起，功名顯朝廷，位都統，顧不得而全忠得之，頗悵恨。

translations.literal: Pu considered himself the earlier riser, his achievements renowned at court, his rank that of overall commander—yet he could not obtain it while Quanzhong did, and he was much aggrieved.
translations.idiomatic: Pu thought himself the earlier champion, his fame bright at court and his rank that of overall commander—yet Quanzhong got what he could not, and he was deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 全忠使司馬李璠、郭言等東，兵道宿州，遺溥書請假道。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent marshals Li Fan and Guo Yan east; the army passed through Xuzhou, and he sent Pu a letter requesting passage.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent marshals Li Fan and Guo Yan east; the army passed through Xuzhou, and he wrote Pu asking leave to march through.

sentences.zh: 溥辭不可，間其墮，以兵襲之。

translations.literal: Pu refused, saying it could not be; when their guard slackened he attacked with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pu refused permission; when their guard lapsed he struck with troops.

sentences.zh: 言戰甚力，解而還。

translations.literal: Yan fought fiercely and broke away to return.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yan fought hard, broke contact, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 全忠怨，自是連歲略徐、泗，師不弛甲。

translations.literal: Quanzhong nursed resentment; from then on year after year he raided Xu and Si, his armies never doffing armor.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong nursed a grudge; from then on he raided Xu and Si year after year, and his armies never laid aside their armor.

sentences.zh: 全忠自將及其郊，未得誌，引去。

translations.literal: Quanzhong personally led troops to the outskirts of the city but did not achieve his aim and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong led the army himself to the city's edge but failed to achieve his aim and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 溥窮，乞師於李克用。

translations.literal: Pu, at bay, begged troops from Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Pu begged Li Keyong for troops.

sentences.zh: 克用為攻碭山，朱友裕救之，各亡其大將。

translations.literal: Keyong attacked Mount Dang on his behalf; Zhu Youyu came to the rescue, and each side lost a major general.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong attacked Mount Dang for him; Zhu Youyu came to the rescue, and each side lost a senior general.

sentences.zh: 友裕進攻宿州，不能拔。

translations.literal: Youyu pressed the attack on Suzhou but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu pressed the attack on Suzhou but could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 時大順元年也。

translations.literal: This was the first year of the Datong era.
translations.idiomatic: This was the first year of the Datong era.

sentences.zh: 明年，丁會築堤閼汴水，灌宿郛，三月，拔之，使劉瓚守。

translations.literal: The next year Ding Hui built a dike to block the Bian River and flood Suzhou's walls; in the third month it fell, and Liu Zan was left to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ding Hui dammed the Bian River to flood Suzhou's walls; in the third month the city fell, and Liu Zan was left to hold it.

sentences.zh: 而溥將劉知俊引兵二千降全忠，軍益不振。

translations.literal: Pu's general Liu Zhijun led two thousand troops to surrender to Quanzhong, and the army grew ever more dispirited.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's general Liu Zhijun then led two thousand men over to Quanzhong, and the army grew ever more dispirited.

sentences.zh: 民失田作，又大水薦饑，死喪十七以上。

translations.literal: The people lost their fields and labor; moreover great floods brought repeated famine—death and loss exceeded seven in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The people lost their fields and livelihood; great floods brought famine after famine, and more than seven in ten died.

sentences.zh: 乃請和於全忠，全忠約徙地而罷兵。

translations.literal: He then sued for peace with Quanzhong; Quanzhong agreed to withdraw troops in exchange for territorial concessions.
translations.idiomatic: He then sued for peace with Quanzhong, who agreed to halt the war if Pu ceded territory.

sentences.zh: 昭宗以宰相劉崇望代之，授溥太子太師。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong replaced him with chancellor Liu Chongwang and appointed Pu Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong replaced him with Chancellor Liu Chongwang and made Pu Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 溥慮去徐且見殺，惶惑不受命，諭軍中固留，有詔聽可。

translations.literal: Pu feared that leaving Xuzhou he would be killed; distraught, he refused the appointment and urged the army to keep him firmly in place; an edict permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: Pu feared that if he left Xuzhou he would be killed; distraught, he refused the post and asked the army to keep him in place, and an edict allowed it.

sentences.zh: 泗州刺史張諫聞溥已代，即上書請隸全忠，納質子焉。

translations.literal: Si prefect Zhang Jian heard Pu had been replaced and immediately memorialized asking to be placed under Quanzhong, sending a hostage son.
translations.idiomatic: When Si prefect Zhang Jian heard Pu had been replaced, he at once memorialized asking to come under Quanzhong and sent a hostage son.

sentences.zh: 溥既復留，諫大懼，全忠為表徙鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Once Pu was retained again, Jian was greatly afraid; Quanzhong memorialized to transfer him to prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu was kept in office after all, Jian was terrified; Quanzhong memorialized to move him to prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 諫畏兩怨集己，乃奔楊行密。

translations.literal: Jian feared resentment from both sides converging on him and fled to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Jian feared anger from both sides would fall on him and fled to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密以諫為楚州刺史，並其民徙之，以兵屯泗。

translations.literal: Xingmi made Jian prefect of Chuzhou, moved the people together with him, and stationed troops at Si.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi made Jian prefect of Chuzhou, moved the people with him, and garrisoned troops at Si.

sentences.zh: 朱友裕率軍攻溥，嬰城不出。

translations.literal: Zhu Youyu led an army against Pu; Pu closed the walls and would not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youyu led an army against Pu, who shut the city and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 有語全忠曰：「軍行非吉日，故師無功。」

translations.literal: Someone told Quanzhong: "The army marched on an inauspicious day, hence the campaign has failed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Quanzhong, "The army marched on an ill-omened day, and that is why the campaign has failed.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣參謀徐璠至軍責諭，友裕答曰：「溥困且破，乃徇妖辭，士心墮矣。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent staff officer Xu Fan to the army to rebuke and instruct; Youyu replied: "Pu is trapped and nearly broken—yet you indulge superstitious talk, and the soldiers' hearts have fallen."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent staff officer Xu Fan to the army to rebuke him; Youyu answered, "Pu is trapped and nearly broken, yet you heed superstitious talk—the soldiers' hearts have fallen."

sentences.zh: 焚其書，督餫饋，急攻之，溥將徐汶出降。

translations.literal: He burned the document, pressed for supply convoys, and attacked urgently; Pu's general Xu Wen surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the letter, pressed for supplies, and attacked hard; Pu's general Xu Wen came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 溥求救於朱瑾。

translations.literal: Pu begged rescue from Zhu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Pu begged Zhu Jin for help.

sentences.zh: 全忠自以兵屯曹，將去，留精騎數千授霍存曰：「事急，可倍道趨之。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong himself encamped at Cao with troops and was about to leave; he left several thousand elite horsemen with Huo Cun and said, "If matters grow urgent, you may march at double speed to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong himself camped at Cao with his army and was about to leave; he left several thousand picked horsemen with Huo Cun and said, "If things grow urgent, march at double speed to reach them.

sentences.zh: 瑾兵二萬與溥合，攻友裕，存引兵疾戰，瑾、溥還壁。

translations.literal: Jin's twenty thousand troops joined Pu and attacked Youyu; Cun led troops into swift battle, and Jin and Pu fell back behind their walls.
translations.idiomatic: Jin brought twenty thousand men to join Pu and attacked Youyu; Cun rushed into battle, and Jin and Pu fell back behind their walls.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，霍存敗，死之。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; Huo Cun was defeated and died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again the next day; Huo Cun was beaten and killed.

sentences.zh: 進逼友裕，友裕堅營不出，瑾食盡，還兗州。

translations.literal: They pressed closer on Youyu; Youyu held his camp firm and would not come out; Jin's provisions ran out and he returned to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed Youyu hard, but Youyu held his camp and would not come out; Jin's food ran out and he returned to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 全忠使龐師古代友裕，溥分兵固保石佛山，師古攻拔之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Pang Shigu to replace Youyu; Pu divided troops to hold Shifo Mountain firmly; Shigu attacked and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Pang Shigu to replace Youyu; Pu split his forces to hold Shifo Mountain, and Shigu stormed and took it.

sentences.zh: 自是完壘不戰。

translations.literal: From then on Pu fortified his ramparts and fought no more.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he repaired his walls and fought no more.

sentences.zh: 王重師、牛存節等梯其堞以入，溥徙金玉與妻子登燕子樓，自焚死，實景福二年。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongshi, Niu Cunjie, and others scaled the parapet to enter; Pu moved gold, jade, his wife and children to ascend Swallow Tower, and burned himself to death—this occurred in the second year of the Jingfu era.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongshi, Niu Cunjie, and others scaled the battlements to enter; Pu moved gold, jade, his wife and children up Swallow Tower and burned himself to death—in the second year of Jingfu.

sentences.zh: 全忠遂有其地，私置守焉。

translations.literal: Quanzhong thereupon took possession of that territory and privately installed a garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong thereupon seized the territory and on his own authority posted a garrison.

sentences.zh: 朱宣，宋州下邑人。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan was a man from Xiayi in Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan came from Xiayi in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父以豪猾聞裏中，坐鬻鹽抵死。

translations.literal: His father was known in the village for boldness and cunning and was executed for the crime of selling salt illicitly.
translations.idiomatic: His father had a local reputation for swagger and sharp dealing and was executed for illicit salt trafficking.

sentences.zh: 宣亡命去青州，為王敬武牙軍。

translations.literal: Xuan fled as an outlaw to Qingzhou and served as a personal guard soldier under Wang Jingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan fled to Qingzhou as a fugitive and joined Wang Jingwu's personal guard corps.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之亂，敬武遣將曹存實率兵西入關，而宣為軍候，道鄆州。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of Huang Chao's rebellion, Jingwu dispatched the general Cao Cunshi to lead troops west through the passes; Xuan served as army scout, passing through Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the upheaval of Huang Chao's rebellion, Jingwu sent General Cao Cunshi west through the passes with an army, while Xuan served as army scout en route through Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是時，節度使薛崇拒王仙芝戰死，其將崔君裕攝州事。

translations.literal: At that time the military governor Xue Chong had been killed in battle resisting Wang Xianzhi; his general Cui Junyu assumed charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Military Governor Xue Chong had died fighting Wang Xianzhi, and his general Cui Junyu took charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 存實揣知兵寡，襲殺之，據其地，遂稱留後。

translations.literal: Cunshi, discerning that their forces were few, launched a surprise attack and killed him, seized the territory, and thereupon styled himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshi, seeing how thin their defenses were, struck by surprise and killed him, seized the place, and proclaimed himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 以宣功多，署濮州刺史，留總帳下兵。

translations.literal: Because Xuan's contributions were great, he was appointed Prefect of Puzhou, though he remained in command of troops under Cunshi's banner.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of Xuan's outstanding service, Cunshi appointed him prefect of Pu Prefecture while keeping him in command of the troops under his own banner.

sentences.zh: 中和初，魏博韓簡東窺曹、鄆，引兵濟河。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhonghe era, Han Jian of Weibo looked east toward Cao and Yan and led troops across the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhonghe reign, Han Jian of Weibo cast a covetous eye on Cao and Yan and led his army across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 存實迎戰，死於陣，宣收殘卒嬰城。

translations.literal: Cunshi met him in battle and died on the field; Xuan gathered the survivors and tenaciously defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshi met him in battle and fell on the field; Xuan rallied the survivors and held the city in a desperate defense.

sentences.zh: 簡圍之六月，不能拔，引兵去。

translations.literal: Han besieged it for six months but could not take it, then withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Han besieged the city for six months without breaking it, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 僖宗嘉其守，拜宣天平節度使，累加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong praised his defense and appointed Xuan Military Governor of Tianping, repeatedly adding the title of co-administrator of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong commended his defense and made Xuan military governor of Tianping, later also appointing him co-administrator of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 宣有眾三萬，弟瑾勇冠三軍，陰有爭天下心。

translations.literal: Xuan had thirty thousand men; his younger brother Jin's bravery led the whole army, and secretly he harbored ambitions to contend for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan commanded thirty thousand men. His younger brother Jin was the bravest soldier in the army and secretly nursed ambitions to contend for the empire.

sentences.zh: 瑾嗜殘殺，光啟中，求婚於兗州節度使齊克讓，托親迎，載兵竊發，逐克讓，據府自稱留後，天子即授以帥節，兄弟雄張山東。

translations.literal: Jin was addicted to cruel slaughter; in the Guangqi era he sought marriage with the Military Governor of Yanzhou, Qi Kerang, using a betrothal procession as cover, secretly setting out with troops, drove Kerang out, seized the prefectural seat and styled himself acting governor—the Son of Heaven at once granted him the commander's commission, and the brothers flourished powerfully in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was bloodthirsty by nature. In the Guangqi era he sought to marry the daughter of Yanzhou's military governor, Qi Kerang. Under the pretense of fetching his bride, he marched out secretly with troops, drove Kerang from office, seized the provincial seat, and proclaimed himself acting governor. The throne promptly invested him with command, and the brothers dominated Shandong.

sentences.zh: 時秦宗權悉兵攻朱全忠，使秦賢列三十六壁，自將督戰。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Zongquan sent his entire army to attack Zhu Quanzhong, assigning Qin Xian to array thirty-six fortified camps while he personally took command to oversee the battle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin Zongquan threw his full strength against Zhu Quanzhong, with Qin Xian entrenched in thirty-six camps while Qin himself supervised the campaign.

sentences.zh: 全忠大恐，求救於宣。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was greatly alarmed and sought rescue from Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was terrified and appealed to Xuan for help.

sentences.zh: 宣與瑾身率師往擊宗權，宗權敗走。

translations.literal: Xuan and Jin personally led troops to strike Zongquan, and Zongquan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Jin led their armies in person against Zongquan and routed him.

sentences.zh: 全忠厚德宣，兄事之，情好篤密，而內忌其雄，且所據皆勁兵地，欲造怨乃圖之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong treated Xuan with great generosity, addressing him as elder brother; their relations were warm and close, yet inwardly he resented Xuan's might, and moreover the territories he held were all strong-army lands—wishing to create grievances, he then plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong showered Xuan with favors and treated him as an elder brother; their bond seemed close. Inwardly, however, he envied Xuan's power, and the territories Xuan held were all rich in fighting men. Quanzhong sought to manufacture a feud and then move against him.

sentences.zh: 即聲言宣納汴亡命，移書詆讓。

translations.literal: He at once publicly claimed that Xuan was harboring fugitives from Bian and sent a letter denouncing and reproaching him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately accused Xuan of sheltering fugitives from Bian and sent a reproachful letter.

sentences.zh: 宣以新有恩於全忠，故答檄恚望。

translations.literal: Xuan, having just recently rendered favor to Quanzhong, therefore replied to the proclamation with indignant reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, having just saved Quanzhong, replied to the proclamation with angry reproaches.

sentences.zh: 全忠由是顯結其隙，使朱珍先攻瑾，取曹州，壁乘氏。

translations.literal: Quanzhong thereby openly cemented the rift, sending Zhu Zhen first to attack Jin, capture Caozhou, and encamp at Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong thus made the breach open and final. He sent Zhu Zhen to attack Jin first, captured Cao Prefecture, and fortified Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 宣救曹不克，奔還範。

translations.literal: Xuan rushed to rescue Cao but could not succeed and fled back to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rushed to relieve Cao Prefecture but failed and fled back to Yan.

sentences.zh: 範珍圍濮州，宣使弟罕救濮。

translations.literal: Zhen, encamped at Yan, besieged Puzhou; Xuan sent his younger brother Han to rescue Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, from his camp at Yan, besieged Pu Prefecture; Xuan sent his younger brother Han to its relief.

sentences.zh: 全忠自將擊罕，斬之，拔濮州，朱裕奔歸鄆，使珍薄鄆挑戰，宣不出。

translations.literal: Quanzhong personally led troops to attack Han, beheaded him, and captured Puzhou; Zhu Yu fled back to Yan; Quanzhong sent Zhen to press close to Yan and provoke battle, but Xuan did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong marched in person against Han, killed him, and took Pu Prefecture. Zhu Yu fled back to Yan. Quanzhong then sent Zhen to threaten Yan and lure Xuan into battle, but Xuan refused to sally forth.

sentences.zh: 裕為書紿降，導珍入，信之，夜以兵數千傅城。

translations.literal: Yu wrote a letter feigning surrender, guiding Zhen to enter; Zhen believed it, and at night led several thousand troops up to the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yu forged a letter offering surrender and lured Zhen in. Zhen took the bait and at night led several thousand men up to the walls.

sentences.zh: 裕開門，軍入，縣門發，死者數千，縱石擊未入者，殺裨將百餘人。

translations.literal: Yu opened the gate; the army entered; the portcullis dropped; several thousand died; stones were loosed upon those who had not entered, killing more than a hundred staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Yu opened the gates and let the army in, then dropped the portcullis. Thousands were killed, and boulders rained down on those still outside, slaying more than a hundred officers.

sentences.zh: 復取曹，以郭詞為刺史，大將郭銖斬詞奔全忠。

translations.literal: They recovered Cao, appointing Guo Ci as prefect; the great general Guo Zhu beheaded Ci and fled to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered Cao Prefecture and installed Guo Ci as prefect, but the senior general Guo Zhu killed Ci and defected to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 瑾謀悉兵襲汴，全忠乃自攻瑾。

translations.literal: Jin plotted to summon all his troops to raid Bian; Quanzhong thereupon personally attacked Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin planned an all-out strike on Bian, so Quanzhong turned to attack Jin in person.

sentences.zh: 瑾以兵掠單父，與全忠將丁會轉戰，不勝，去。

translations.literal: Jin led troops to plunder Shanfu, battling in turn with Quanzhong's general Ding Hui; he could not prevail and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jin raided Shanfu and fought a running battle with Quanzhong's general Ding Hui but could not win and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景福初，復伐宣，令從子友裕先驅，自繼之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu, Quanzhong again campaigned against Xuan, ordering his nephew Youyu as vanguard while he followed after.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingfu, Quanzhong again marched against Xuan, sending his nephew Youyu ahead while he followed with the main force.

sentences.zh: 次衛南，宣以輕兵夜掩友裕軍，走之，據其營。

translations.literal: Halting south of Wei, Xuan with light troops by night surprised Youyu's army, routed it, and seized his camp.
translations.idiomatic: South of Wei, Xuan struck Youyu's camp at night with a light force, routed him, and took his encampment.

sentences.zh: 全忠未知，運糧以入，乃覺，走瓠河，與友裕相失，距濮十五里舍。

translations.literal: Quanzhong did not yet know; he sent grain transport in and only then realized; he fled to Hulu River, lost contact with Youyu, and encamped fifteen li from Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong did not yet know what had happened and sent supply trains forward before he realized the danger. He fled to the Hulu River, lost contact with Youyu, and made camp fifteen li from Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明日，友裕乃至。

translations.literal: The next day Youyu at last arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu did not rejoin him until the next day.

sentences.zh: 宣留濮州。

translations.literal: Xuan remained at Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan stayed at Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 全忠令友裕馳壯騎諜鄆虛實，身將而北。

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered Youyu to gallop elite horsemen to reconnoiter Yan's strength and weakness, while he personally led troops north.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Youyu ahead with mounted scouts to probe Yan's defenses while he marched north in person.

sentences.zh: 會宣引還，縱兵戰，全忠南走，絕塹去，幾不脫，大將多死。

translations.literal: Just as Xuan was leading his forces back, he unleashed troops in battle; Quanzhong fled south, crossed the ditch to escape, nearly failed to get away, and many of his senior generals died.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was marching back when he turned and gave battle. Quanzhong fled south, scrambling across the ditch to escape. He barely got away, and many of his senior commanders were killed.

sentences.zh: 乃謀持久僥極取宣，歲一再暴其鄙，奪之食，俘其工織，有存者。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then plotted a war of attrition hoping at the limit to take Xuan; once or twice each year he raided Xuan's borders, seized his grain, captured his artisans and weavers—some survived.
translations.idiomatic: He then settled on a strategy of attrition, hoping to wear Xuan down in the end. Once or twice a year he raided Xuan's territory, seized his grain, and carried off his craftsmen and weavers; some of these captives survived.

sentences.zh: 宣令賀瑰守濮州，為友裕所攻，委城走。

translations.literal: Xuan ordered He Gui to hold Puzhou; attacked by Youyu, he abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan left He Gui to defend Pu Prefecture, but when Youyu attacked, He Gui abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 友裕進擊徐州，時溥求援於宣，戰不勝而還，溥遂亡。

translations.literal: Youyu pressed the attack on Xuzhou; Shi Pu sought aid from Xuan, fought without victory and returned; Pu thereupon perished.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu pressed on against Xu Prefecture. Shi Pu appealed to Xuan for help, but their combined forces were beaten back, and Pu was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 全忠即遣龐師古攻齊州，宣、瑾皆戍以兵，久不下。

translations.literal: Quanzhong at once dispatched Pang Shigu to attack Qizhou; Xuan and Jin both garrisoned it with troops, and for a long time it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong immediately sent Pang Shigu against Qi Prefecture. Xuan and Jin both sent reinforcements, and the siege dragged on without success.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年，全忠身往，薄清河結壘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianning, Quanzhong went in person, pressed close to the Qing River and established fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianning, Quanzhong took the field in person, drew up near the Qing River, and built fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 宣、瑾三分其兵出擊之，全忠迎戰東阿，南風急，汴軍居下，甚懼。

translations.literal: Xuan and Jin divided their forces three ways and sallied to attack; Quanzhong met them in battle at Dong'e; the south wind blew fiercely, and the Bian army held the lower ground and was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Jin split their army three ways and attacked. Quanzhong met them at Dong'e. A fierce south wind blew, and the Bian forces, fighting from low ground, were badly shaken.

sentences.zh: 俄而風返，全忠得縱火焚其旁，熛薰漲天，宣等大北。

translations.literal: Before long the wind shifted; Quanzhong was able to set fires and burn their flank; flames and smoke billowed to the sky; Xuan and the others suffered a great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Then the wind swung around. Quanzhong set fire to their flank, and flames and smoke filled the sky. Xuan's forces were routed.

sentences.zh: 是夏，全忠壁曹州南，宣薄戰，禽其將三人。

translations.literal: That summer Quanzhong encamped south of Caozhou; Xuan pressed close and fought, capturing three of his generals.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Quanzhong encamped south of Cao Prefecture. Xuan closed in and fought, taking three of his generals prisoner.

sentences.zh: 全忠還。

translations.literal: Quanzhong returned.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，使朱友恭擊兗州，瑾堅壁，乃塹而守。

translations.literal: The next year he sent Zhu Yougong to attack Yanzhou; Jin held fast behind his walls, then dug moats and maintained the defense.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent Zhu Yougong against Yan Prefecture. Jin kept to his walls, then dug entrenchments and dug in.

sentences.zh: 宣饟瑾，友恭奪其糧。

translations.literal: Xuan sent provisions to Jin; Yougong seized the grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent supplies to Jin, but Yougong intercepted and seized the grain.

sentences.zh: 全忠自軍單父。

translations.literal: Quanzhong personally encamped at Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong took the field himself from Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 會宣求救於李克用，友恭退壁曹南。

translations.literal: Just then Xuan sought rescue from Li Keyong; Yougong withdrew and encamped south of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan appealed to Li Keyong for help, and Yougong pulled back to fortify south of Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 數月，全忠自伐宣，刈其麥，敗克用將李承嗣等，乃還。

translations.literal: After several months Quanzhong personally campaigned against Xuan, reaped his wheat, defeated Li Keyong's generals Li Chengsi and others, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later Quanzhong marched against Xuan in person, cut his wheat crop, defeated Li Keyong's generals Li Chengsi and others, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宣追之，大鈔曹州。

translations.literal: Xuan pursued him and raided Caozhou on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan pursued and plundered Cao Prefecture on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 其秋，全忠復攻鄆，壁梁山。

translations.literal: That autumn Quanzhong again attacked Yan, encamping at Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Quanzhong attacked Yan again and fortified at Liang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 宣、克用挑戰，全忠設伏破之，斬首數千級，引而南。

translations.literal: Xuan and Keyong challenged him to battle; Quanzhong set an ambush and defeated them, beheading several thousand, then led his forces south.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Keyong offered battle, but Quanzhong ambushed and routed them, taking several thousand heads, then marched south.

sentences.zh: 克用躡全忠後，至柏和，大寒，全忠軍多死。

translations.literal: Keyong followed on Quanzhong's heels; reaching Bohe, the cold was intense and many in Quanzhong's army died.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong pursued Quanzhong as far as Bohe. In the bitter cold, many of Quanzhong's soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 不閱月，復圍兗州，因略地龔丘。

translations.literal: In less than a month he again besieged Yanzhou, and meanwhile overran the territory of Gongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was besieging Yan Prefecture again while overrunning Gongqiu.

sentences.zh: 賀瑰以奇兵擊全忠輜重，不及，戰鉅野東，瑰大敗，見禽，師無孑余。

translations.literal: He Gui with a surprise force struck at Quanzhong's baggage train but failed to overtake it; they fought east of Juye; Gui was utterly defeated, captured alive, and not a single soldier remained.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui led a flanking force against Quanzhong's supply train but failed to intercept it. They fought east of Juye. Gui was crushed, taken alive, and his army was annihilated to the last man.

sentences.zh: 軍道大陂，風暴起，全忠曰：「豈殺人有遺邪？」

translations.literal: On the march the army passed a great marsh; a violent storm arose; Quanzhong said, "Can it be that when killing men some are spared?"
translations.idiomatic: On the march the army crossed a great marsh and a violent storm broke. Quanzhong said, "When you kill men, can any be left alive?"

sentences.zh: 乃搜軍中，復斬數千人，風亦止，執瑰示城下。

translations.literal: He then searched through the army and beheaded several thousand more; the wind also stopped; he had Gui seized and displayed him below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He then combed the ranks and executed several thousand more. The storm abated, and he paraded the captive He Gui beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 瑾之兄瓊守齊州，見勢屈，以州歸全忠，結同姓歡。

translations.literal: Jin's elder brother Qiong held Qizhou; seeing the tide turn against them, he surrendered the prefecture to Quanzhong and pledged fraternal joy as men sharing the same surname.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's elder brother Qiong held Qi Prefecture. Seeing defeat inevitable, he surrendered the prefecture to Quanzhong and pledged brotherhood as fellow Zhu clansmen.

sentences.zh: 全忠許之，輕騎至軍，全忠勞苦加禮，因使招瑾。

translations.literal: Quanzhong agreed; Qiong came to the camp with a light escort; Quanzhong treated him with laborious courtesy and thereby had him summon Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong agreed. Qiong rode to the camp with a small escort, was received with every honor, and was sent to persuade Jin to surrender.

sentences.zh: 瑾領精騎鬲池笑語如平生歡，乃使將胡規偽送款，欲得瓊躬上符節。

translations.literal: Jin led elite horsemen to Geci Pool, laughing and talking as in the joy of former days; he then sent the general Hu Gui to feign submission, wishing to have Qiong come in person to deliver the tally and commission.
translations.idiomatic: Jin rode with an elite guard to Geci Pool, chatting as though they were old friends at ease. He then sent General Hu Gui with a false offer of surrender, demanding that Qiong deliver the credentials in person.

sentences.zh: 全忠不之虞，瑾伏壯士橋下，瓊單騎至，方交語，士突起，掖瓊以入，斬其首棄城下，汴軍大震。

translations.literal: Quanzhong did not suspect him; Jin hid stalwart men beneath the bridge; Qiong came alone on horseback; just as they were exchanging words the men sprang up, seized Qiong and pulled him inside, beheaded him and cast the head below the walls; the Bian army was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong suspected nothing. Jin had armed men hidden beneath the bridge. When Qiong rode up alone and they began to talk, the men burst out, dragged Qiong inside, beheaded him, and threw his head down before the walls. The Bian army was stunned.

sentences.zh: 全忠恚，數日乃去。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was enraged; only after several days did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was furious and did not withdraw for several days.

sentences.zh: 三年，克用使其將李瑭以兵屯莘援宣，為羅弘信所破。

translations.literal: In the third year Keyong sent his general Li Tang to encamp at Shen with troops to aid Xuan, but he was defeated by Luo Hongxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Li Keyong sent General Li Tang to garrison Shen in support of Xuan, but Luo Hongxin defeated him.

sentences.zh: 全忠大喜，度宣可困，遣龐師古伐宣，宣逆戰，敗於馬頰河。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was greatly pleased, reckoned that Xuan could be cornered, and dispatched Pang Shigu to campaign against Xuan; Xuan met him in battle and was defeated at the Ma'yi River.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was delighted, judged that Xuan could at last be broken, and sent Pang Shigu against him. Xuan met the attack but was beaten at the Ma'yi River.

sentences.zh: 師古迫其西門，兵不出。

translations.literal: Shigu pressed close to the western gate; no troops came out.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu pushed to the western gate, but no one sallied forth.

sentences.zh: 全忠之攻宣，凡十興師，四敗績。

translations.literal: In Quanzhong's campaigns against Xuan, he raised armies ten times in all and suffered defeat four times.
translations.idiomatic: In all, Quanzhong had launched ten campaigns against Xuan and lost four of them.

sentences.zh: 宣才將皆盡，益內沮，度不能與全忠確，則固守，增堞深溝為不可逼。

translations.literal: Xuan's talented generals were all exhausted; he grew ever more disheartened within; reckoning he could not match Quanzhong in a decisive contest, he then held fast, raised the parapets and deepened the moats to make the city impossible to force.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had exhausted his best commanders and lost heart. Seeing he could not beat Quanzhong in open battle, he dug in, raised his walls, and deepened his moats until the city seemed unassailable.

sentences.zh: 明年，葛從周密造舟於塹，師人逾而升。

translations.literal: The next year Ge Congzhou secretly built boats in the moat; soldiers crossed over and climbed up.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ge Congzhou secretly built boats in the moat, and his men crossed over and scaled the walls.

sentences.zh: 宣出奔，為民所縛，追至，執以獻，全忠斬之而納其妻。

translations.literal: Xuan fled; the common people bound him; pursuing troops overtook him, seized him and presented him as captive; Quanzhong beheaded him and took his wife into his household.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan fled but was seized by local villagers. Pursuers caught up, took him captive, and delivered him to Quanzhong, who executed him and took his wife.

sentences.zh: 使師古攻兗州。

translations.literal: He sent Shigu to attack Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shigu to attack Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二月，食盡，瑾自出督芻粟，轉掠豐、沛間，而子用貞及大將康懷英等舉城降。

translations.literal: In the second month provisions were exhausted; Jin went out in person to oversee fodder and grain, turning to plunder between Feng and Pei; meanwhile his son Yongzhen and the great generals Kang Huaiying and others surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: By the second month food was gone. Jin rode out to gather fodder and foraged between Feng and Pei, while his son Yongzhen and senior generals including Kang Huaiying surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 瑾引麾下走沂州，刺史尹懷賓不納，乃趨海州，刺史朱用芝以其眾與瑾奔楊行密，行密迎之高郵，解玉帶以賜，表領徐州節度使，畀以兵。

translations.literal: Jin led his followers to flee to Yizhou; the prefect Yin Huaibin would not admit them; he then pressed on to Haizhou; the prefect Zhu Yongzhi went with his forces together with Jin to flee to Yang Xingmi; Xingmi welcomed him at Gaoyou, removed his jade belt and bestowed it on him, memorialized that he be appointed Military Governor of Xuzhou, and granted him troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fled with his followers to Yi Prefecture, but Prefect Yin Huaibin turned him away. He pressed on to Hai Prefecture, where Prefect Zhu Yongzhi joined him with his troops in flight to Yang Xingmi. Xingmi received Jin at Gaoyou, gave him his own jade belt, petitioned to make him military governor of Xu Prefecture, and supplied him with an army.

sentences.zh: 師古、從周以兵七萬討行密，瑾敗之清口，擊殺師古，而從周還，師至淠水，方涉，瑾追及，殺傷溺死幾盡。

translations.literal: Shigu and Congzhou with seventy thousand troops campaigned against Xingmi; Jin defeated them at Qingkou, struck and killed Shigu; Congzhou returned; when his army reached the Pi River and was mid-ford, Jin overtook them; killed, wounded, and drowned, nearly all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu and Congzhou marched against Xingmi with seventy thousand men. Jin routed them at Qingkou and killed Shigu. As Congzhou retreated across the Pi River, Jin caught him mid-crossing and slaughtered his army almost to the last man by blade, wound, and drowning.

sentences.zh: 瑾事行密尤盡力。

translations.literal: Jin served Xingmi with especial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Jin thereafter served Xingmi with unstinting loyalty.

sentences.zh: 孫儒，河南河南人。

translations.literal: Sun Ru was a native of Henan in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru came from Henan in Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 以趫卞橫裏中，隸忠武軍為裨校，與劉建鋒善。

translations.literal: For swiftness and fierceness he was feared across the village; he entered service in the Zhongwu Army as a staff officer and was on good terms with Liu Jianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Known in his village for speed and brutal force, he enlisted in the Zhongwu Army as a junior officer and became close to Liu Jianfeng.

sentences.zh: 黃巢亂，以兵屬秦宗權，為都將。

translations.literal: During Huang Chao's rebellion he entered Qin Zongquan's service with his troops and became a chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao's rebellion broke out, he brought his men into Qin Zongquan's ranks and rose to chief commander.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，宗權遣儒攻東都，留守李罕之出奔，儒焚宮闕，屠居人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Zongquan dispatched Ru to attack the Eastern Capital; the provisional governor Li Hanzhi fled; Ru burned the palace halls and slaughtered the inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangqi, Zongquan sent Ru against the Eastern Capital. The interim governor Li Hanzhi fled. Ru burned the palace complex and massacred the populace.

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使諸葛爽與儒戰洛水，爽敗，儒亦東圍鄭州。

translations.literal: The Military Governor of Heyang, Zhuge Shuang, fought Ru at the Luo River; Shuang was defeated; Ru also pressed east to besiege Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang Military Governor Zhuge Shuang fought Ru on the Luo River and was beaten. Ru then turned east to besiege Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠屯中牟救之，不敢前。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong encamped at Zhongmou to rescue it but dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong camped at Zhongmou to relieve the city but dared not move forward.

sentences.zh: 儒眾夜登城，刺史李璠走，儒進拔河橋，遂取河陽，留後諸葛仲方出奔。

translations.literal: Ru's host by night scaled the walls; the prefect Li Fan fled; Ru advanced and captured the Yellow River bridge, then took Heyang; the acting governor Zhuge Zhongfang fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's troops scaled the walls by night. Prefect Li Fan fled. Ru pushed forward, took the Yellow River bridge, and seized Heyang, driving out Acting Governor Zhuge Zhongfang.

sentences.zh: 全忠壁河陰，儒掠汴鄙，全忠兵卻，屯胙城東南，列偽旗鼓疑之，儒乃還。

translations.literal: Quanzhong fortified at Heyin; Ru plundered the borders of Bian; Quanzhong's troops fell back and encamped southeast of Zuocheng, arraying false flags and drums to confuse him; Ru then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong fortified Heyin while Ru raided Bian's outskirts. Quanzhong pulled back to Zuocheng southeast and set out dummy banners and drums to deceive him, and Ru withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會全忠與宗權戰，宗權敗走。

translations.literal: Just then Quanzhong fought Zongquan; Zongquan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: About then Quanzhong fought Zongquan and routed him.

sentences.zh: 儒聞，殺孟人，流屍於河，焚井邑，乃去。

translations.literal: When Ru heard, he killed the people of Meng, floated corpses on the river, burned wells and settlements, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Ru heard the news, he slaughtered the people of Meng, cast corpses into the river, burned towns and villages, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宗權又遣儒鈔淮南，乘高駢之亂，儒留濠州。

translations.literal: Zongquan again sent Ru to raid Huainan; seizing on the turmoil of Gao Pian, Ru remained at Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan sent Ru raiding into Huainan. Taking advantage of the chaos around Gao Pian, Ru stationed himself at Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會楊行密得揚州，宗權使弟宗衡爭淮南，以儒為副，建鋒為前鋒。

translations.literal: Just then Yang Xingmi had taken Yangzhou; Zongquan sent his younger brother Zongheng to contest Huainan, with Ru as second in command and Jianfeng as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi had just taken Yangzhou. Zongquan sent his brother Zongheng to contest Huainan, with Ru as second in command and Jianfeng as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 儒常曰：「丈夫不能苦戰萬里，賞罰繇己，奈何居人下，生不能富貴，死得廟食乎？」

translations.literal: Ru often said, "A man who cannot fight arduous battles for ten thousand li, with rewards and punishments at his own command—why dwell beneath others? If in life one cannot know wealth and rank, can one in death receive temple offerings?"
translations.idiomatic: Ru often said, "What sort of man fights his way ten thousand li with reward and punishment in his own hands, yet serves under another? If you cannot be rich and honored in life, what temple offerings will you earn in death?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，汴兵攻蔡，宗權召之，儒稱疾不往，宗衡督之。

translations.literal: Before long Bian troops attacked Cai; Zongquan summoned him; Ru claimed illness and would not go; Zongheng pressed him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bian forces attacked Cai Prefecture. Zongquan summoned Ru, but Ru pleaded illness and refused to come. Zongheng pressed him to march.

sentences.zh: 即大會帳下，酒酣，斬宗衡，並其眾。

translations.literal: He at once held a great assembly of those under his banner; when the wine was deep, he beheaded Zongheng and absorbed his forces.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered his officers for a feast and, at the height of the drinking, executed Zongheng and took over his troops.

sentences.zh: 與建鋒、許德勛等盟。

translations.literal: He allied with Jianfeng, Xu Dekun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He entered an alliance with Jianfeng, Xu Dekun, and the others.

sentences.zh: 有騎七千，因略定傍州，不淹旬，兵數萬，號「土團白條軍」。

translations.literal: He had seven thousand cavalry; thereby he overran and secured neighboring prefectures; in less than ten days his troops numbered tens of thousands; they were styled the "Local Corps White-Stripe Army."
translations.idiomatic: With seven thousand horsemen he overran the neighboring prefectures, and in less than ten days his force swelled to tens of thousands. They called themselves the "Local White-Stripe Corps."

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，悉兵攻宣州，行密取淮南，儒還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he sent his entire army to attack Xuanzhou; Xingmi took Huainan; Ru returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longji he marched in full strength against Xuan Prefecture while Xingmi seized Huainan, forcing Ru to turn back.

sentences.zh: 行密走，始得潤、常、蘇三州，兵益強，使建鋒守潤、常。

translations.literal: Xingmi fled; he had just secured the three prefectures Run, Chang, and Su; his army grew ever stronger; he had Jianfeng guard Run and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi had been driven back but had just taken Run, Chang, and Su Prefectures. His strength grew, and he left Jianfeng to hold Run and Chang.

sentences.zh: 全忠約行密圖之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong entered an agreement with Xingmi to plot against Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong made a pact with Xingmi to bring Ru down.

sentences.zh: 儒謀定江南，乃北爭天下，畏全忠搗虛，乃遣人卑辭厚賄，全忠薦於朝，詔授淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Ru planned to secure Jiangnan, then contend for the empire in the north; fearing Quanzhong would strike at his rear, he sent men with humble words and rich bribes; Quanzhong recommended him to the court, and an edict appointed him Military Governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Ru meant to consolidate the south first, then turn north for the empire. Fearful that Quanzhong would strike his rear, he sent envoys with humble flattery and rich gifts. Quanzhong recommended him to court, and he was appointed military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 大順元年，行密取潤州，以安仁義守之，常州以李友守之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dashun, Xingmi took Runzhou, assigning An Renyi to hold it; for Changzhou he assigned Li You to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dashun, Xingmi took Run Prefecture and left An Renyi in charge; he placed Li You in command at Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 儒怒，三分其軍度江，建鋒復拔常、潤，仁義走。

translations.literal: Ru was enraged; he divided his army three ways and crossed the river; Jianfeng again captured Chang and Run; Renyi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ru was furious. He split his army three ways, crossed the Yangtze, and Jianfeng recaptured Chang and Run Prefectures while Renyi fled.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣將龐從等軍十萬奄至高郵，儒悉師禦之，故仁義間取潤州，劉威、田頵等敗建鋒於武進，取常州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong dispatched the generals Pang Cong and others with an army of one hundred thousand to descend suddenly on Gaoyou; Ru sent his entire force to resist; therefore Renyi in the interval retook Runzhou; Liu Wei, Tian Jun, and others defeated Jianfeng at Wujin and recovered Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Pang Cong and others with a hundred thousand men in a sudden drive on Gaoyou. Ru committed his whole army to meet them, and in the meantime Renyi snatched back Run Prefecture while Liu Wei and Tian Jun defeated Jianfeng at Wujin and retook Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 杭州錢镠將沈粲自蘇州奔儒，行密諸將在潤、常者，皆為建鋒所逐，仁義、頵棄潤州走。

translations.literal: Qian Liu's general Shen Can of Hangzhou fled from Suzhou to Ru; all of Xingmi's generals who were at Run and Chang were driven off by Jianfeng; Renyi and Jun abandoned Runzhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Can, a general of Hangzhou's Qian Liu, defected from Suzhou to Ru. Jianfeng drove out every one of Xingmi's commanders still at Run and Chang, and Renyi and Jun abandoned Run Prefecture and fled.

sentences.zh: 明年，儒引兵自京口轉戰，召建鋒皆行。

translations.literal: The next year Ru led his army from Jingkou in continuous fighting and summoned Jianfeng to march with him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Ru marched from Jingkou in a rolling campaign and called Jianfeng to join him with all his forces.

sentences.zh: 行密諸將屯險者，聞儒至，皆走。

translations.literal: Xingmi's generals holding defiles, hearing that Ru had come, all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Every Xingmi general holding a strong position fled when he heard Ru was coming.

sentences.zh: 頵、威等合兵三萬，邀儒黃池。

translations.literal: Jun, Wei, and others united thirty thousand men and intercepted Ru at Huangchi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun and Liu Wei united thirty thousand men and blocked Ru at Huangchi.

sentences.zh: 儒遣馬殷擊走之。

translations.literal: Ru sent Ma Yin to attack and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Ru sent Ma Yin to attack and rout them.

sentences.zh: 儒營廣德，乘勝至東溪，淮人大恐。

translations.literal: Ru encamped at Guangde, pressed his victory to Dongxi, and the people of Huai were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Ru encamped at Guangde, pressed his victory to Dongxi, and panic spread through the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 行密遣臺濛屯西溪，自引軍逆戰。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent Tai Meng to camp at Xixi and himself led the army to meet the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi posted Tai Meng at Xixi and personally led his army to meet Ru in battle.

sentences.zh: 儒軍圍之數重，黑雲將李簡以騎馳之，行密乃免。

translations.literal: Ru's army surrounded them in many rings; Li Jian of the Black Cloud Corps charged with cavalry, and Xingmi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's army ringed them round and round until Li Jian of the Black Cloud Corps charged with cavalry and Xingmi broke free.

sentences.zh: 儒遂圍宣州，行密乞師於錢镠。

translations.literal: Ru then besieged Xuancheng, and Xingmi begged troops from Qian Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Ru then laid siege to Xuancheng, and Xingmi appealed to Qian Liu for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 會溪潦暴湧，廣德、黃池諸壁皆沒，儒分兵取和、滁二州。

translations.literal: Just then mountain floods surged; the forts at Guangde, Huangchi, and elsewhere were all submerged, and Ru divided his forces to take He and Chu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden mountain floods swept away the camps at Guangde and Huangchi; Ru split his army and seized Hezhou and Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其秋，儒焚揚州，引而西，傳檄遠近，號五十萬，旌旗相屬數百里，所過燒廬舍，殺老弱以給軍。

translations.literal: That autumn Ru burned Yangzhou and marched west, sending proclamations far and near claiming five hundred thousand men; banners and flags stretched for hundreds of li; wherever he passed he burned houses and killed the old and weak to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Ru burned Yangzhou and marched west, proclaiming an army of five hundred thousand; his banners stretched for hundreds of li; everywhere he went he burned homes and slaughtered the old and weak to feed his troops.

sentences.zh: 行密懼，將遁去。

translations.literal: Xingmi was afraid and was about to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was terrified and ready to flee.

sentences.zh: 戴規曰：「儒軍數敗，今掃地而至，決死於我，若吾遣降者間至揚州，撫尉衣食，使儒軍聞其家尚完，人人思歸，不戰可禽也。」

translations.literal: Dai Gui said, "Ru's army has been beaten many times; now they sweep in resolved to die against us. If we send surrendered men secretly to Yangzhou to comfort them with food and clothing, so that Ru's troops hear their families are still safe, every man will think of returning, and we can take them without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Gui said, "Ru has lost battle after battle; now he sweeps in ready to die against us. Send men who have surrendered into Yangzhou in secret—feed and clothe them, let Ru's soldiers hear their families are safe, and every man will yearn to go home. We can take them without a fight."

sentences.zh: 行密乃遣親將入揚州，取儒營糧數十萬斛以稟饑民。

translations.literal: Xingmi then sent trusted generals into Yangzhou, took several hundred thousand hu of grain from Ru's camps, and distributed it to the starving people.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent trusted officers into Yangzhou, seized hundreds of thousands of hu of grain from Ru's depots, and fed the starving populace.

sentences.zh: 儒屯廣德，陶雅以騎軍破儒前鋒，屯嚴公臺。

translations.literal: Ru encamped at Guangde; Tao Ya with cavalry broke Ru's vanguard and encamped at Yanggong Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Ru camped at Guangde; Tao Ya's cavalry shattered his vanguard and took position at Yanggong Terrace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，頵、威與儒決戰，皆大敗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jun and Wei fought a decisive battle with Ru and were both badly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Tian Jun and Liu Wei met Ru in a decisive battle and were crushed.

sentences.zh: 儒連屯稍西，行密使陶雅屯潤州，扼其歸路。

translations.literal: Ru moved his successive camps slightly west; Xingmi had Tao Ya camp at Runzhou to block his line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Ru shifted his camps westward; Xingmi posted Tao Ya at Runzhou to cut off his retreat.

sentences.zh: 景福元年，儒復圍宣州，屯陵陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingfu, Ru again besieged Xuancheng and encamped at Lingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingfu, Ru again besieged Xuancheng and encamped at Lingyang.

sentences.zh: 行密戰不利，謀出奔，時劉威方系獄，且死，行密窮，更召問計，對曰：「儒焚倉隤壘以來，糧盡將為我禽。

translations.literal: Xingmi fought without success and planned to flee; at the time Liu Wei was in prison and near death; Xingmi, at his wits' end, summoned him again for counsel, and he replied, "Since Ru burned his stores and tore down his ramparts on the march, his grain is exhausted and he will soon be ours.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was losing and planned flight. Liu Wei lay in prison near death; in desperation Xingmi called him back for advice. Wei said, "Ru burned his granaries and dismantled his walls as he marched—his supplies are gone and we will have him soon.

sentences.zh: 若勁兵背城，坐制其困。」

translations.literal: If you send crack troops with their backs to the city and sit to control his distress."
translations.idiomatic: Put your best troops with their backs to the wall and wait—his desperation will do the rest."

sentences.zh: 李神福亦請據險邀儒糧。

translations.literal: Li Shenfu also asked to hold defiles and intercept Ru's grain.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu also urged holding the passes to cut Ru's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 行密乃分兵攻廣德，壁而絕饟道。

translations.literal: Xingmi then divided his forces to attack Guangde, fortified positions, and cut off the supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi split his forces to strike Guangde, fortified the passes, and severed Ru's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 軍適大疫，儒病痁，遣建鋒、殷鈔諸縣。

translations.literal: The army happened to suffer a great pestilence; Ru fell ill with malaria and sent Jianfeng and Yin to levy the counties.
translations.idiomatic: A plague swept the army; Ru fell ill with malaria and sent Jianfeng and Yin to forage the counties.

sentences.zh: 行密知城下兵寡，乃晨出，率仁義、頵背城決戰，破五十壁。

translations.literal: Xingmi knew the troops below the city were few; at dawn he went out, led Renyi and Jun in a decisive battle with their backs to the wall, and broke fifty camps.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Ru's camp was thin, Xingmi marched out at dawn with An Renyi and Tian Jun, fought with the city at their backs, and smashed fifty encampments.

sentences.zh: 會暴澍且冥，儒軍大敗。

translations.literal: Just then a violent downpour fell at dusk, and Ru's army was badly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden storm burst at dusk, and Ru's army collapsed in defeat.

sentences.zh: 儒病甚，股弁不能興。

translations.literal: Ru was gravely ill and could not rise from his couch.
translations.idiomatic: Ru was desperately ill and could not rise from his bed.

sentences.zh: 頵執儒獻行密，諸將皆降。

translations.literal: Jun seized Ru and presented him to Xingmi; all the generals surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun seized Ru and brought him before Xingmi; Ru's generals all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 儒就刑於市，見劉威曰：「中君之謀。」

translations.literal: Ru was executed in the marketplace; seeing Liu Wei he said, "I fell into your lordship's stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Ru was executed in the marketplace. Seeing Liu Wei he said, "I walked straight into your plan."

sentences.zh: 儒嘗引鑒搔首曰：「此頭不久當入京師。」

translations.literal: Ru had once taken a mirror and scratched his head, saying, "This head will soon enter the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Ru had once gazed in a mirror and tugged his hair, saying, "This head will soon reach the capital."

sentences.zh: 至是，傳首闕下。

translations.literal: And now his head was sent to the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: And now his head was sent to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 建鋒、殷哭之，相語曰：「公常有誌廟食，吾等有土，當廟以報德。」

translations.literal: Jianfeng and Yin wept for him and said to each other, "Our lord always wished for temple offerings; when we hold territory we should raise a temple to repay his grace."
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng and Yin wept and said to one another, "Our lord always wanted a temple sacrifice; when we hold land we must build him a shrine to repay his kindness."

sentences.zh: 及殷據湖南，表儒贈司徒、樂安郡王，立廟以祀。

translations.literal: When Yin held Hunan, he memorialized to posthumously award Ru the title of Minister of Works and Prince of Le'an commandery, and established a temple to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin ruled Hunan, he memorialized to posthumously name Ru Minister of Works and Prince of Le'an, and built a temple in his honor.
